explanation: 该论文主要关注地球系统稳定性和气候失控风险，特别是社会因素如何影响地球系统的反馈机制和人类应对气候变化的能力。虽然与环境和地球系统相关，但并未涉及大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析或气溶胶反演等具体技术或应用。
authors: James G Dyke;Laurie Laybourn;Jesse F Abrams
title: Manage derailment risks to avoid Hothouse Earth
abstract: The risk of a ‘Hothouse Earth’ trajectory has become increasingly prominent in debates about Earth system stability and climate overshoot. Existing analyses primarily focus on biophysical feedbacks that may amplify warming beyond direct anthropogenic forcing. We argue the concept has not previously incorporated how social destabilisation lowers the effective threshold at which biophysical tipping dynamics become self-sustaining, independently of further anthropogenic forcing and so undermines the capacity for planetary stewardship. We define ‘derailment risk’ as the possibility that escalating Earth system disruption weakens the social, political, and economic conditions required to sustain mitigation, adaptation, and ecological restoration. Such risks emerge when climate impacts contribute to a wide range of challenges, including debt crises, institutional erosion, political fragmentation, supply-chain instability, and declining public support for environmental action. These reinforcing feedbacks may reduce humanity’s capacity to respond even before biophysical tipping thresholds are crossed. We therefore extend the Hothouse Earth framework by incorporating social dynamics into the Earth system stability landscape. We propose a three-stage framework for assessing and managing derailment risks: conceptual mapping of socio-biophysical feedbacks; anticipatory resilience-building interventions; responsive governance strategies for periods of escalating instability. We conclude that planetary stewardship should prioritise maintaining and expanding collective agency under worsening Earth system stress.

title: CORRIGENDUM: How scientists’ collective climate advocacy affects public trust in scientists and voting behavior (2025 Environ. Res. Lett. 20 014043)

explanation: 该研究涉及太阳辐射修正技术及其对区域经济的影响，虽然不直接涉及大气环境遥感技术，但太阳辐射修正与大气成分和气候变化密切相关，因此与大气环境遥感技术的应用领域相关。
authors: Jenny Bjordal;Evelien van Dijk;Henri Cornec;Anthony A Smith;Trude Storelvmo
title: Regional economic impacts and emission responses under solar radiation modification
abstract: Solar radiation modification (SRM) has been proposed as a potential tool to limit increases in global or regional temperatures caused by anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. While previous research has extensively examined the climate system’s response to various SRM strategies, as well as their aggregate economic consequences, the spatial distribution of economic impacts has received less attention. In this study, we use NorESM2-Disaggregated Integrated Assessment Model—an Earth System Model coupled to a high-resolution integrated assessment model—to assess the economic impacts, measured in gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, in an idealised SRM scenario where incoming solar radiation is reduced by 1%. Our results suggest that, relative to a baseline without SRM, most countries experience economic gains under SRM, with only a few countries facing negative impacts. Low-income countries tend to see the largest benefits, reducing disparities in GDP per capita across countries relative to the baseline. However, reduced damages and smaller disparities in GDP per capita are accompanied by a ‘moral hazard’ effect, in that SRM leads to higher emissions, which may in turn cause additional adverse effects not captured here. These findings highlight potential trade-offs between economic benefits, the distribution of economic impacts, and increased emissions relevant for SRM governance.

explanation: 该论文使用卫星观测数据（如Landsat、ECOSTRESS和MODIS）来分析大型数据中心集群对周围环境的热影响，涉及空气质量监测、地表温度变化和能量平衡分析，属于大气环境遥感技术的范畴。
authors: Jiawei Jing
title: Satellite observations and energy balance constrain the thermal footprint of a hyperscale data-centre cluster
abstract: Whether hyperscale data centres (DCs) warm their surroundings divides current evidence: a coarse-resolution satellite preprint attributes ∼2 °C of land-surface-temperature (LST) warming to facilities worldwide (Marinoni et al 2026 arXiv: 2603.20897v3), while peer-reviewed transects near Phoenix measure +0.7–0.9 °C of near-ground air warming a few hundred metres downwind (Sailor et al 2026 J. Eng. Sustain. Bldgs. Cities7 024501). Prospective anthropogenic-heat models remain untested against long-term observations, and no major DC market assesses local temperature impact before construction. We provide the first ex-post, controlled satellite test for Japan’s largest DC concentration, the Inzai and Tama clusters near Tokyo, whose staggered build-out (twelve facilities, 2011–2025) yields a three-phase event study with replication. The test combines daytime Landsat (2013–2026), 70 m day/night ECOSTRESS and 1 km MODIS with matched pre-2013 controls, facility-level energy disclosures and minimum-detectable-effect analysis, gated by an air-temperature energy-balance ceiling (∼0.35 °C, cluster scale, night) that bounds LST a fortiori. Commissioning cools the daytime LST by 1.8 °C–2.2 °C—significant under all three reference types, a radiative-property signal opposite in sign to the viral claim. Deep-night facility-scale LST changes are indistinguishable from zero (bounded below ∼0.6 °C–1.2 °C), and the cluster-scale night LST bound (0.24 °C–0.29 °C, autocorrelation-corrected, two platforms) closes beneath the air-temperature ceiling. The exclusion of warming at the claimed magnitude rests primarily on energy balance—+ 2 °C, even in air, would require 6–43 times the available waste heat—with observations supplying consistent bounds at every scale they resolve. Arid- and continental-climate consistency checks (Phoenix and DeKalb) reproduce the decomposition: in both, night surface warming is largely in place during construction—before any server load—and matches neighbouring non-DC development; conversion, not exhaust. Near-source air warming is real where rejection density is high and climates dry; kilometre-scale surface warming from waste heat is unattainable. The protocol is the ex-post verification tool siting regimes lack.

authors: Lakshani Gunawardhana;Margaret M Busse
title: Modeling freshwater use for direct lithium extraction from geothermal brines in the Salton Sea
abstract: Global lithium demand is projected to more than double by 2035, to about 715 kt per year (3.8 Mt lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) per year) under the International Energy Agency Stated Policies Scenario, intensifying the need for new, sustainable extraction routes. Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from geothermal brines is of particular interest because co-location with closed-loop geothermal operations avoids the large land footprint of evaporation ponds and the carbon intensity of hard-rock mining. The Salton Sea Known Geothermal Resource Area (SS-KGRA) hosts geothermal plants with co-located pilot-scale DLE facilities and is one of the most advanced regions for geothermal lithium extraction. Though these operations are expected to reduce land and carbon intensity, they require freshwater inputs across multiple unit operations; this demand has been reported only as facility-wide aggregates, without process-level resolution, even though the SS-KGRA lies in an arid region where water supply is largely committed to agriculture. Existing estimates do not track the internal fate of process water, which determines the net volume drawn from external sources. Herein, we present LiHydroSim, a process-based model that translates publicly available process descriptions into a facility-level freshwater balance through a three-layer architecture separating gross unit-operation demand, internal recovery, and net external supply. Applied to a representative adsorption-based facility processing 7000 gallons per minute of geothermal brine, the model estimates net external freshwater demand of 1719 acre-feet per year (152 m  t LCE; 0.12 AF/t LCE), below the 189–355 m  t LCE (0.15–0.29 AF/t LCE) reported by Salton Sea developers, consistent with auxiliary demands outside the process boundary. The eluant for lithium elution dominates the water balance, accounting for 92% of gross internal process-water demand, while internal recycling offsets roughly one third of that gross demand. Total demand depends mainly on eluant volume: across two patent-specified operating modes, it ranges from 870 to 1719 acre-feet per year.

explanation: 该论文使用遥感技术（Landsat数据）和变化检测算法（LandTrendr）来评估红树林的恢复轨迹和碳汇潜力，涉及遥感技术在环境监测中的应用，因此与大气环境遥感技术相关。
authors: Yuxuan Zhao;Tong Li;Bohan Zheng;Xinyu Wang;Yifan Wang;Qiyue Zhang;Zheng Xiao;Yuxin Chen;Nan Xu;Yi Li
title: Evaluating mangrove establishment trajectories and carbon recovery potential using a spatial age-based framework
abstract: Mangrove restoration is a vital nature-based solution for climate change mitigation and biodiversity conservation. However, large-scale mangrove restoration success is predominantly evaluated using area-based metrics, which fail to capture the complex temporal trajectories of forest structural and functional recovery. Stand age directly determines structural heterogeneity and carbon stocks, making it a key indicator for monitoring recovery trajectories and estimating carbon stocks. We developed a spatial age-based framework to map established mangrove stands and quantify the existing carbon stock and remaining potential. To this end, we combined an optimized LandTrendr change-detection algorithm with age-stratified logistic growth models using Landsat time-series data. We generated a 30-m resolution age map of all established mangroves from 2000 to 2023 across tropical Hainan Island, China. Our results identified 337 ha of established mangroves as of 2023. Notably, >50% (173 ha) of the detected stands are ⩽7 years old yet have already attained 43% of mature forest carbon stocks, whereas only 4% of them have reached ⩾15 years. Under continued protection, these forests are expected to store an estimated 33 668 Mg C (27 971–38 902 Mg C), with the greatest potential concentrated in the Dongzhaigang area. Conversely, the limited extent of older forests (4% of the established area) already secures significant recovered carbon stocks, warranting urgent protection. This contrast underscores the necessity of differentiated management strategies calibrated to both restoration scale and stand development stage. Ultimately, this spatially explicit framework informs evidence-based management to improve restoration outcomes and provides actionable baselines for national carbon credit markets.

explanation: 该论文主要关注城市适应性和治理框架，涉及公平、正义和社会机构，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）没有直接关系。
authors: Md Nazirul Islam Sarker;Zekui Ning;Wenlong Feng;Md Abdullah Al Mamun
title: Adapting with justice: a governance framework for equitable urban resilience beyond the environmental justice triad
abstract: Urban adaptation can redistribute protection, public investment, land value, and displacement risk across neighborhoods and social groups. This scoping review, reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR, synthesized scholarship on justice, governance, and equitable urban resilience. Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for English-language publications from January 2000 through February 2026, supplemented by backward reference checking. After duplicate removal, title/abstract screening, and full-text assessment, 79 studies were included. A combined deductive–inductive thematic synthesis, organized with MAXQDA Analytics Pro, identified three interlocking governance pillars: justice architectures, accountable co-production, and context-tuned strategies. Across the included studies, equitable adaptation was repeatedly discussed in relation to enforceable rights, distributional targeting, meaningful community authority, attention to compound and context-specific risks, anti-displacement safeguards, and durable operations and maintenance. By contrast, consultation without decision authority and adaptation investment without housing protection were described as risks for reproducing exclusion, unequal access, and climate gentrification. The review translates these patterns into five assessable governance checkpoints: rights and intergenerational accountability, distributional targeting, shared decision authority, scale and compound-risk fit, and anti-displacement protection and benefit durability. The resulting framework is an analytically derived and testable governance framework rather than a validated causal model. It provides a structured basis for evaluating whether urban adaptation is environmentally effective, socially just, institutionally accountable, and durable over time.

explanation: 该论文研究了不同道路车辆排放清单对下游空气质量、暴露、健康和公平性评估的影响。它使用了数值空气质量模型（如InMAP）来模拟交通相关污染物的浓度和影响，并探讨了不同排放清单和空间分辨率对模拟结果的影响。这与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）密切相关，因为这些都是通过遥感技术和模型来评估大气污染和空气质量的重要手段。
authors: Kyan K Shlipak;Victoria A Lang;Martha Santiago;Christopher W Tessum;Daniel E Horton
title: Impact of different on-road vehicle emissions inventories on downstream air quality, exposure, health, and equity assessments
abstract: Emissions from on-road vehicles are a pervasive source of air pollution, contributing to inequitable pollutant exposure and adverse health outcomes. Numerical air quality models are used to characterize traffic-related pollutant concentrations and impacts. However, model outputs rely on underlying emissions inventories whose formulations can differ substantially. Here, we leverage the widely used Intervention Model for Air Pollution (InMAP) to examine how four different on-road emissions inventories used at three different spatial resolutions (1, 1.3, and 4 km) influence simulated fine particulate matter (PM2.5) population exposure, health impacts, and equity outcomes in a freight-heavy urban setting—the Greater Chicago Region. We find that population-weighted exposure and attributable mortality differ up to 72% and 69% across inventories, compared to only 14%–17% across resolutions. While all inventories result in higher estimated PM2.5 exposure and mortality among Black, Hispanic, and Asian populations compared to non-Hispanic White populations, the magnitude and relative ordering of disparities across racial groups vary with both inventory choice and spatial resolution. Furthermore, we demonstrate that characterizing exposure inequities using emissions colocation can yield substantially different disparity estimates (up to 20%) from pollutant concentration-based estimates due to atmospheric transport and chemistry— a divergence that likely represents a lower bound given InMAP’s reduced-complexity parameterizations. This work builds on recent studies showing that model resolution influences air quality, health, and equity assessments by demonstrating that on-road emissions inventory choice introduces even greater differences than spatial resolution.

authors: María Aguilera-Vidal;Thomas Wahl;José A Jiménez
title: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies rainfall in extreme compound rainfall-wave events in the NW Mediterranean
abstract: The concurrent occurrence of extreme rainfall and energetic wave conditions can generate compound coastal hazards with impacts exceeding those produced by either driver alone. Although recent studies have identified changes in rainfall-wave extremes along the northwestern Mediterranean coast, whether these changes can be attributed to anthropogenic climate remains unclear. Here, we investigate the anthropogenic influence on compound rainfall-wave extremes using five initial-condition ensemble members of the CMIP6 MRI-ESM2.0 model from the Detection and Attribution Model Intercomparison Project, comparing factual (ALL) and counterfactual (NAT) experiments over 1961–2020. Changes in dependence and joint return periods are assessed using Kendall’s τ-b and copula-based analyses. No robust anthropogenic signal is detected in the observed strengthening of rainfall-wave dependence, as neither its temporal evolution nor the change in dependence structure identified in ERA5 is consistently reproduced across the ensemble. In contrast, the ALL-NAT comparison suggests an anthropogenic contribution to rainfall intensification in the most extreme compound events, while wave changes remain small and variable across realizations. For example, fitted estimates associate a rainfall-wave combination of P24h ≈320 mm and Hs ≈4 m with joint return periods of approximately 50 years under NAT and 25 years under ALL. This comparison is indicative, with its magnitude subject to uncertainties in event sampling, marginal fitting, and copula estimation that have yet to be quantified. Agreement with ERA5 supports the model’s representation of baseline characteristics, although further evaluation would strengthen confidence in its response to external forcing. Overall, the findings suggest rainfall intensification within the model framework, while the associated frequency change should be interpreted with caution.

explanation: 该论文使用卫星影像（PlanetScope imagery）和深度学习技术（deep learning）来评估乌克兰战区防护林（shelterbelt）的退化情况。这属于遥感技术在环境监测（如森林、植被变化监测）中的应用，与大气环境遥感技术中的卫星观测、地表覆盖变化分析等密切相关，因此该论文与大气环境遥感技术主题相关。
authors: Viktor Myroniuk;Yevhenii Khan;Oleksandr Sovakov;Maksym Matsala;Andrii Lashchenko;Anatolii Makarevych;Andrii Terentiev
title: Deep learning reveals severe shelterbelt degradation in eastern Ukraine due to the war
abstract: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 has caused extensive damage to forests, particularly in eastern and southern regions with sustained combat, where field shelterbelts have often been used as cover and subsequently heavily destroyed. This study presents a systematic region-scale assessment of pre-war shelterbelt area and war-related loss between 2021 and 2025 using 3 m PlanetScope imagery and deep learning. We evaluated three input datasets—monthly PlanetScope RGB mosaics, multiseasonal PlanetScope RGB stacks, and surface reflectance (SR) PlanetScope imagery—in combination with two semantic segmentation architectures: a convolutional U-Net with a ResNet-34 encoder and a transformer-based SegFormer with a MiT-B0 backbone. Across all input configurations, the U-Net consistently outperformed SegFormer, achieving the highest F1 scores. Monthly RGB mosaics delivered accuracy comparable to more complex multiseasonal and SR inputs in pixel-based evaluation and are a cost-efficient option for mapping narrow shelterbelts. The RGB-based model trained on July 2021 mosaics reached an F1 score of 0.71 and retained values of 0.58–0.67 for other months of the same leaf-on season. Temporal transfer to 2025 resulted in lower but still reasonable performance with F1 scores of 0.53–0.63. Error-adjusted mapping estimated the shelterbelt area in 2021 at 254 ± 14.5 thousand ha, equivalent to a mean density of 2.6 ha km−2. By 2025, this area had been reduced by approximately 41 thousand ha, or 16% of the pre-war area. Losses were strongly concentrated along frontlines where local losses exceeded 1.5 ha km−2 compared to an average loss of 0.5 ha km−2 across the entire study area. The resulting maps complement the existing forest monitoring framework in Ukraine and provide a spatially explicit basis for prioritizing post-war remediation and assessing losses in protective functions and carbon accumulation.

explanation: 该论文研究了海水与臭氧反应产生的气体，以及这种过程如何随海洋生物的季节性变化而变化。这些发现有助于改进空气质量气候预测，揭示了一个重要的自然大气气体来源。因此，它与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、大气成分分析）密切相关。
authors: Frances E. Hopkins;Daniel P. Phillips;Yinghao Chen;Peter S. Liss;Mingxi Yang
title: Uncovering the seasonal trends of VOC production from ozonolysis of seawater
abstract:
Our study reveals how the surface ocean produces gases when it reacts with ozone. We found that this process changes in response to seasonal changes in ocean biology. By testing fresh seawater and natural organic material, we showed that shifts in plankton and related chemistry strongly affect which gases form. These results help improve predictions of air quality and climate by revealing a natural source of important atmospheric gases. 
 Large uncertainty exists in the role that the ocean plays as a net source for atmospheric volatile organic carbon (VOC) compounds, in part because of poorly quantified processes near the air–sea interface. Laboratory studies imply that heterogeneous reactions of ozone at the ocean surface may be a key source of VOCs to the marine atmosphere, but the representativeness of such experiments for the chemically complex surface ocean waters is unclear due to limited field evidence. Here, we determined the production ratios of select VOCs formed during ozonolysis of fresh, natural seawater from laboratory experiments under turbulent conditions using a proton-transfer-reaction quadrupole mass spectrometer (PTR-MS). To quantify seasonal variability, near-surface water samples were collected from a temperate marine station during different seasons and measured for ozone-driven VOC production ratios. In all experiments, out of the VOCs monitored the dominant products of ozonolysis were m/z 69 (C5H9+), followed by m/z 59 (acetone/propanal) and m/z 45 (acetaldehyde). Clear seasonal differences in VOC production imply that marine biogeochemistry likely drives the availability and composition of VOC precursors. Further ozonolysis experiments using diluted VOC precursors (senescent algal culture, fatty acids, certified natural organic matter (NOM)) resulted in different VOC production compared to those using natural seawater. Our results show that ocean biogeochemical cycling is a key driver of variability in ozone-driven VOC production at the sea surface.

explanation: 该论文研究了气溶胶在垂直方向上的分布，使用了激光雷达等地面测量技术，并探讨了边界层动力学对气溶胶垂直结构的影响，这与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）密切相关。
topic_words: ['aerosol vertical distributions', 'lidar', 'boundary layer dynamics', 'air quality monitoring', 'atmospheric composition analysis']
authors: Bo Chen;Seth A. Thompson;Brianna H. Matthews;Milind Sharma;Ron Li;Anita D. Rapp;Christopher J. Nowotarski;Sarah D. Brooks
title: Aerosol vertical distributions shaped by boundary layer dynamics in a coastal urban environment: insights from the TRACER campaign
abstract:
This paper studies how aerosols, tiny particles suspended in the air, are distributed at different heights in the atmosphere. We use lidar and other ground-based measurements to estimate aerosol vertical profiles. We also develop a simple mathematical equation that can recreate the observed profile shape using a few adjustable parameters. Finally, we examine several case studies and explore how the profile shape is related to boundary-layer structure and atmospheric conditions. 
 Aerosol vertical distributions are a major source of uncertainty in quantifying aerosol–cloud–climate interactions. Using observations collected during the 2022 TRACER campaign in Houston, Texas, we investigate how atmospheric boundary layer dynamics shape the vertical structure of aerosol populations in a coastal urban environment. Our lidar retrieval combines micropulse lidar backscatter with ground-based aerosol measurements to obtain aerosol concentration profiles. A compact framework for describing aerosol vertical profile shape is needed to examine factors that influence aerosol vertical distributions and to represent them in model parameterizations or remote sensing retrievals. We introduce a parameterized fitting function for characteristic S-shaped aerosol profiles, with fitted parameters that represent aerosol-layer depth and stratification strength. This parameterization is applied to case studies demonstrating how boundary-layer dynamics, including turbulent mixing, capping inversion strength, and sea-breeze circulations, influence aerosol vertical distributions. Case studies show that aerosol concentrations decrease rapidly near strong capping inversions, the depth of the lower aerosol layer changes with boundary-layer growth and collapse, and sea-breeze passage produces strong coastal–inland differences as maritime air replaces continental aerosol. Analysis of the six-month dataset shows weak but statistically significant positive relationships between daytime boundary layer height and fitted aerosol layer depth, and between the local potential temperature gradient near the aerosol layer top and fitted stratification strength parameter. Finally, we demonstrate an approach for estimating aerosol profile shape from boundary-layer height and potential-temperature gradients using the fitted parameterization. These results show that this parameterization provides simple, interpretable diagnostics for linking aerosol profile shape to boundary-layer dynamics.

explanation: 该研究探讨了2,4-二硝基酚在大气环境中的转化机制，涉及气相和气-水界面的反应动力学，以及其与羟基自由基、臭氧和二氧化氮的相互作用。这些内容与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测和大气成分分析密切相关。
authors: Chenlei Wang;Ran Li;Jiaxing Sun;Zihan Zhang;Nan Zhao;Leilei Liu;Zuju Ma;Maoxia He;Jianfei Sun
title: Unveiling the multiphase fate of 2,4-dinitrophenol on aerosols: interfacial hydration modulates competing oxidation pathways and predicted toxicity indicators
abstract:
2,4-Dinitrophenol reacts mainly with hydroxyl radicals and ozone, while solvation and nitro groups affect its reactivity. A key radical intermediate reacts with O2 and NO2. Adsorption varies non-monotonically with hydration. Quantitative structure activity relationship (QSAR) predictions show that some ozonolysis products may have higher mutagenicity and developmental toxicity than the parent compound, highlighting the need to assess transformation products. 
 This study elucidates the mechanisms of selected transformation pathways of 2,4-dinitrophenol (2,4-DNP) using an integrated computational framework. In the gas phase, the calculated initial reactions with hydroxyl radicals (•OH) and ozone (O3) are kinetically more favorable than the direct reaction with nitrogen dioxide radical (•NO2), which is kinetically hindered. In the aqueous phase, solvation substantially modifies the calculated reaction kinetics, and the cumulative electron-withdrawing effect of the two nitro substituents lowers the O3 reaction rate coefficient by approximately three orders of magnitude relative to mononitrocatechol. For the key radical intermediate generated by •OH addition, hydrogen atom abstraction (HAA) by O2 is kinetically favored over the competing •NO2 pathway based on the calculated barriers and an illustrative comparison of effective rates under representative atmospheric concentrations. At the gas-aqueous interface, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations show a non-monotonic dependence of 2,4-DNP adsorption on hydration in the idealized C60/water system, with adsorption strengthening at moderate hydration and weakening at high hydration. Finally, QSAR calculations predict that certain ozonolysis products exhibit higher predicted Ames mutagenicity and developmental toxicity indicators than the parent compound, indicating product-specific changes in predicted toxicity profiles during oxidation. These screening-level predictions require experimental validation. These findings provide molecular-level mechanistic insights into selected transformation pathways and interfacial interactions involving 2,4-DNP and motivate further experimental investigation of its transformation products and their toxicological properties.

explanation: 该论文研究了地球关怀任务（EarthCARE）在监测热带 anvils 云动力方面的潜力，涉及卫星观测技术和大气成分分析，因此与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Hirohiko Masunaga
title: A preliminary analysis of tropical anvil-cloud dynamics in EarthCARE
abstract:
EarthCARE is the first space mission with the capability to measure vertical motion inside clouds. This work assesses the utility of EarthCARE observations for studying the vertical motion of air in tropical anvil clouds. The findings are encouraging in that EarthCARE not only provides robust estimates of vertical air motion but has the potential to quantify the horizontal motion as well. This will be useful for better understanding how anvil clouds are formed and sustained over time. 
 The vertical motion in tropical anvil clouds is crucial for understanding their maintenance and evolution but is notoriously difficult to observe. This work explores the potential utility of EarthCARE in revealing previously unobserved aspects of anvil clouds using the radar-only (2A.CPR_CLP) and radar-lidar synergy (2B.AC_CLP) products. Composite vertical profiles of cloud fraction sorted by ice water path (IWP) are constructed as a statistical representation of anvil clouds and deep convection. In-cloud vertical air motion as estimated from Doppler measurements reveals that intense updraft penetrating within deep convection gives way to a weaker ascent in anvil clouds. The radar-only product slightly underestimates the ascent in anvil clouds relative to the radar-lidar product due to a difference in the particle size distribution, while the overall spatial pattern of vertical air motion remains consistent. Diagnostic horizontal wind is then derived from the vertical motion estimates under mass conservation in composite vertical-horizontal space. The resulting wind vector field emerges as an overturning mesoscale circulation constituted of a mid-tropospheric inflow and an upper-tropospheric outflow. The present findings, although preliminary, confirm the promising potential of EarthCARE observations for investigating the anvil cloud dynamics.

explanation: 该研究探讨了天气类型对夜间臭氧增加的影响，涉及气象驱动因素和物理机制，与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测和大气成分分析密切相关。
authors: Huanpeng Wang;Liya Fan;Xuejiao Deng;Haomin Huang;Daiqi Ye
title: Impacts of synoptic circulation types on nocturnal ozone increase in the North China Plain: meteorological drivers and physical mechanisms
abstract:
This study investigates how weather types drive nocturnal ozone increase. We resolve four primary weather types in the North China Plain: A-type (57.89 %), S-type (19.88 %), WNE-type (14.04 %), and C-type (8.19 %). Driven by these weather systems, high-pressure subsidence (A-type), cold pool subsidence and shallow convection (C-type), synoptically-driven wind shear (S-type and WNE-type) act as key drivers, facilitating the intrusion of ozone-rich air to the surface. 
 Nocturnal ozone (O3)  increase (NOI) has become common worldwide, raising the risk of O3 pollution. While weather types serve as critical drivers of NOI, their specific dynamic influences remain poorly understood. Using ground observations and reanalysis datasets, this study identified the relationship between weather types and NOI days in a representative city in the North China Plain, and revealed the meteorological characteristics and physical mechanisms driving these events. During 2021–2023, 370–444 NOI days were observed, with the occurrence predominantly concentrated between 00:00 and 06:00 local time (69.53 %). After screening, a total of 171 representative NOI days were finally identified to characterize the overall occurrence of local NOI events. Based on the Lamb-Jenkinson method, the representative NOI days were classified into four primary weather types: A-type (57.89 %), S-type (19.88 %), WNE-type (14.04 %), and C-type (8.19 %). A-type was dominated by high-pressure anticyclones with calm conditions, whereas C-type was controlled by low-pressure systems and influenced by moist airflows. S-type was located in the transition zone between high and low pressure, influenced by southern geostrophic winds, and WNE-type was characterized by high-pressure systems with W-N-E geostrophic flows. Distinct mechanical triggers for NOI were further resolved for different types: A-type is dominated by high-pressure subsidence; C-type is driven by cold-pool downdrafts and convective motions; whereas both S-type and WNE-type are primarily controlled by synoptically-driven intense wind shear. This study elucidates the diverse dynamical pathways of weather-driven NOI, providing mechanistic insights for improving O3 forecasting and mitigation strategies in urban environments.

authors: Ales Kuchar;Matthias Stocker;Alistair Bell;Bruno Lehner;Jessica Kult-Herdin;Gabriel Chiodo;Timofei Sukhodolov;Eugene Rozanov;Gunter Stober;Harald E. Rieder
title: Evidence for Hunga-Tonga eruption influence on the anomalously strong Northern-Hemisphere stratospheric polar vortex in 2024/2025
abstract:
We investigated why the Northern Hemisphere winter polar vortex became unusually strong in the winter of 2024/2025. Using satellite and reanalysis datasets, and model simulations, we found that extra water erupted high in the atmosphere by the 2022 Hunga Tonga eruption led to cooling of polar latitudes of the upper atmosphere, helping the winds aloft intensify. This link suggests such volcanic eruptions can shape winters in the upper atmosphere for several years. 
 The 2022 Hunga Tonga (HT) eruption injected an unprecedented amount of water vapour (WV) into the stratosphere and mesosphere, emerging as a potential multi-year driver of variability in those layers and associated climate feedbacks. Using satellite and reanalysis datasets, and ensemble simulations with the SOCOLv4 model, with and without the HT forcing, we diagnose the chain of processes linking the eruption to the exceptionally strong Northern Hemisphere stratospheric polar vortex (SPV) observed in winter 2024/2025. Satellite data show “tongues” of enhanced WV descending from the mesosphere into the polar stratosphere, collocated with ozone reductions and persistent cold anomalies, alongside a record-strong SPV. Our model with the HT forcing can reproduce the main structure of the descending plume, its effects on chemistry, and the SPV strengthening, albeit with underestimated magnitudes and an earlier onset than observed. Offline radiative transfer calculations indicate that the WV and ozone anomalies drive net radiative cooling over the polar stratosphere, which steepens meridional temperature gradients and thereby intensifies the Arctic polar vortex. The observed 2024/2025 winter thus represents a plausible manifestation of HT-induced vortex variability. Our simulations also predicted the observed shift towards more favorable conditions for sudden stratospheric warmings in the winter 2025/2026 as the WV forcing declines.

title: Sensitivities of a simulated Arctic stratocumulus to aerosol and microphysical parameters
abstract:
Arctic low clouds containing both droplets and ice crystals strongly impact sea ice and therefore require accurate modeling. Using a high-resolution atmospheric model, we found that particle and ice concentrations, alongside ice crystal shape, strongly dictate the simulated cloud. Therefore, these specific properties should be prioritized during future Arctic observational campaigns. Furthermore, atmospheric models must be able to represent a variety of ice crystal shapes. 
 Low-level, mixed-phase clouds are a key component of the Arctic energy budget and can impact the extent and thickness of sea ice. These clouds are influenced by aerosols and microphysical processes that can determine the phase partitioning and thereby cloud lifetime and radiative impacts. Atmospheric models often struggle to represent phase partitioning in Arctic mixed-phase clouds correctly. Aerosol number concentration (ANC), aerosol type (Atype), ice crystal number concentration (ICNC), and ice crystal morphology (ice crystal habit; IChab) have previously been shown to impact phase partitioning in Arctic clouds. We used factorial analysis to rank these parameters according to their explained variance in simulated liquid water path (LWP), ice water path (IWP), and downward longwave radiation at the surface (DWLW) of a slightly supercooled Arctic mixed-phase cloud. Additionally, we analyzed how these parameters affect the final phase state of the simulated cloud. Using MIMICA, the MISU-MIT Cloud Aerosol large-eddy simulation code, we found that ANC was the most important parameter for LWP and DWLW, while ICNC controlled IWP. IChab ranked third for all simulated variables, yet it crucially determined the final phase state of the cloud. The impact of Atype was negligible compared to the other three parameters. Recognizing the limits of relying on a single case study and model, our results suggest that future Arctic field campaigns should prioritize observations of ANC, ICNC, and, crucially, ice habit for slightly supercooled mixed-phase clouds. Models must also represent different ice habits to accurately simulate cloud phase partitioning and its subsequent impact on the Arctic energy budget.

explanation: 该论文研究了多站流星雷达网络中体积速度处理方法，用于大气动力学中的垂直风检索，这与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶检索）密切相关，因为流星雷达是大气遥感的重要工具，可用于监测大气风场和动力学特性。

authors: Loretta Pearl Poku;Gunter Stober;Witali Krochin;Alan Liu;Alexander Kozlovsky;Diego Janches;Jie Zeng;Wen Yi;Hanli Liu;Zishun Qiao;Kaoru Sato;Masaki Tsutsumi;Njål Gulbrandsen;Satonori Nozawa;Mark Lester;Johan Kero;Nicholas Mitchell
title: Comparison of tomographic wind retrievals with different geometric implementations for multistatic meteor radar networks
abstract:
Reliable vertical wind retrieval is essential for understanding atmospheric coupling anddynamics. We present a novel Volume Velocity Processing method in spherical coordinates forthe mesosphere and lower thermosphere, improve physical consistency, and compare results withcurrent state-of-the-art models (VVP, 3DVAR+DIV, JAWARA, and SE-WACCM-X). Resultsshow reduced altitude-dependent biases from incomplete representation of the observationgeometry in mean horizontal and vertical winds. 
 A growing number of multistatic meteor radar networks are being established worldwide. The multistatic geometry with overlapping observation volumes of several meteor radars or passive receivers permits the inference of higher-order kinematic properties of the wind field or even the retrieval of arbitrary wind fields using tomographic algorithms. Furthermore, there is the long-standing question of the reliability of the vertical wind. In this study, we present a novel Volume Velocity Processing in spherical coordinates and perform an initial cross-comparison to previous implementations of the Volume Velocity Processing and the advanced 3DVAR+DIV retrieval. We performed a detailed climatological and multiyear comparison of mean winds, horizontal divergence, relative vorticity, stretching, and shearing deformation using observations of the Nordic Meteor Radar Cluster consisting of the meteor radars at Tromsø, Alta, Kiruna, and Sodankylä. Our results underscore that the spherical implementation of Volume Velocity Processing reduces/minimizes altitude-dependent biases caused by projection errors resulting from an incomplete representation of the observation geometry in the mean horizontal and vertical winds. All algorithms exhibit a very high correlation for the mean horizontal winds, but we found substantial differences in the vertical wind velocity and in the higher-order kinematic properties between the novel algorithm and previous versions of the Volume Velocity Processing.  Furthermore, the novel algorithm reproduces a consistent seasonal pattern of the vertical velocity with upwelling during the hemispheric summer at the altitude of the zonal wind reversal and a corresponding but weaker downwelling during the winter months. The magnitudes of the vertical wind appear to be physically consistent with theoretically expected upward and downward motions and are on the order of a few cm s−1. We also identified a scaling effect of the vertical wind in dependence on the temporal resolution and spatial averaging represented by a circle of influence in the new retrieval, which was confirmed by the measurement response of the 3DVAR+DIV retrieval. Wind data retrieved from SSVP and VVP are compared with the Japanese meteorological reanalysis known as JAWARA and SE-WACCM-X model data. The vertical wind patterns observed by the Nordic Meteor Radar Cluster show strong agreement between the two. Robust vertical wind retrievals obtained with a temporal resolution of 15–30 min and within a spatial domain of approximately 200–250 km centered between all meteor radars provide the best compromise between sampling density and spatial averaging for the Nordic Meteor Radar Cluster.

explanation: 该论文研究了使用无人机在森林生态系统中测量CO2排放的方法，涉及大气成分分析和垂直/水平运输的测量，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Haijiong Sun;Shao-Meng Li;Yifei Wang;Yanrong Yang;Tianran Han;Keyu Chen;Chang Liu;Jietao Zhou;Zeqing Ma;Fengting Yang;Junfei Guo;Xiangyu Gao
title: UAV-based method for measuring CO2 emissions in forest ecosystems
abstract:
We designed a drone system to measure forest carbon dioxide exchange in difficult terrain. It measures carbon dioxide and wind on loop flights and vertical climbs to estimate both vertical exchange and sideways transport. At a subtropical plantation in southern China, results matched an eddy covariance tower. Sideways transport often dominated early morning, while midday uptake prevailed. Total uncertainty was about fifteen percent, making this a flexible complement to fixed towers. 
 This study addresses the difficulty of accurately quantifying CO2 emissions in forest ecosystems due to spatial heterogeneity, complex terrain, and the combined effects of horizontal and vertical transport. A methodology for quantifying 3-D CO2 emissions using an unmanned aerial vehicle was developed, evaluated, and applied to a forest ecosystem. The measurement platform was integrated with a high-precision closed-path CO2 analyzer to measure CO2 mole fractions and a calibrated ultrasonic anemometer to measure wind vectors, together with profile measurements of temperature and pressure. Within a mass-balance framework, the instrumented platform was flown along horizontal loops at multiple heights together with vertical ascent flight tracks, acquiring data along the flight tracks that were used to quantify horizontal advective and vertical turbulent carbon dioxide emission components, respectively. The method was applied at a subtropical plantation forest and evaluated against fluxes derived using a nearby eddy covariance flux tower. Validation against long-term CO2 flux measurements from the permanently installed eddy covariance system shows that vertical CO2 fluxes derived from the airborne observations agree well with the tower observations across seasons, with a correlation coefficient of 0.9 based on 168 paired flux estimates collected between May 2023 and December 2024. Measurements collected along the horizontal box-pattern flight paths further reveal diurnal variations in local canopy-air CO2 mass transport: lateral advection dominates in the early morning, whereas vertical uptake prevails under well-mixed midday conditions. Sensitivity analysis of emission intensities across control volumes with different horizontal dimensions (50 × 50, 100 × 100, and 150 × 150 m2) and a constant vertical extent of 50 m revealed stronger scale dependence during autumn mornings, indicating significant spatial heterogeneity in CO2 emissions. Uncertainty assessment suggests that the total relative uncertainty of the emission estimates derived using this approach is typically approximately 30 %, with wind-field measurement as the main error source. Overall, the proposed approach provides a flexible and reliable method for analyzing near-surface 3-D CO2 transport over structurally heterogeneous forests and complex terrain, helping to overcome the limited spatial coverage of traditional flux towers and remote sensing.

explanation: 该论文研究利用多波长卫星测量技术检索平流层气溶胶大小分布，特别是针对平流层硫酸盐和烟雾气溶胶。文中详细描述了如何使用卫星观测数据（如SAGE III/ISS）来获取气溶胶的物理和光学特性，并与地面实测数据进行对比验证。这与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，涉及卫星观测、气溶胶分布分析和质量控制等方面。
topic_words: ['stratospheric aerosol', 'SAGE III/ISS', 'bimodal aerosol size distributions', 'satellite measurements', 'pyroCb']
authors: Vishal Bagadia;Cheng-Hsuan Lu
title: Retrieval of bimodal aerosol size distributions for stratospheric sulfate and smoke aerosols using multi–wavelength satellite measurements
abstract:
A new approach to retrieve stratospheric aerosol size distributions is developed to characterize smoke aerosol properties. Pyrocumulonimbus can strongly perturb stratospheric aerosol concentrations. Simulations are conducted to describe stratospheric aerosol properties for bimodal lognormal distributions. Observations from SAGEIII/ISS are used to determined stratospheric smoke aerosol size distributions and optical and microphysical properties and are validated against in situ measurements. 
 Pyrocumulonimbus events (pyroCb) are a natural driver of stratospheric aerosol variability by injecting smoke plumes containing aerosols and trace gases into the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere. Smoke aerosols are distinct in their chemical, optical, and microphysical properties from stratospheric sulfate aerosols. A new approach in retrieving the bimodal lognormal aerosol size distribution from stratospheric aerosol observations is developed. Aerosol size distributions inferred from in situ and satellite based studies are used to model stratospheric aerosol properties following a pyroCb event. Synthetic and observational multi–wavelength data from the Stratospheric Aerosol and Gas Experiment III on the International Space Station (SAGE III/ISS) are used to simulate and validate the retrieval method. Aerosol optical and microphysical properties are determined to vary for coarse mode aerosol concentrations totaling more than 0.1 %–1 % of the population. Simulated retrievals show reduced negative bias in number density with retrieval of a bimodal distribution, with limitations from the measurement technique and retrieval persisting in defining the ultrafine aerosol concentrations. Retrieved aerosol size distributions resolve the shape, centers, and range of the synthetic distributions, with retrieved distribution moments consistently within the uncertainty range of the input extinction measurements.Validation of the retrieval algorithm applied to SAGE III/ISS observations is conducted against in situ balloon-borne measurements characterizing aerosol properties following pyroCb events in the northern hemisphere in 2017 and 2020. SAGE III/ISS retrieved aerosol size distributions of stratospheric smoke in these coincident observations display two modes with fine mode median diameters approximately 200–400 nm and coarse mode median diameters of 500–800 nm. Observed aerosol surface area and volume densities are enhanced in the perturbed layers over quiescent conditions and show strong agreement between the SAGE III/ISS retrieved and in situ measured values.

explanation: 该论文研究了烟雾年龄的确定方法，并将其应用于NASA-NOAA FIREX-AQ实地实验，涉及大气成分分析和烟雾传输的遥感技术。烟雾年龄是解释大气成分变化的重要参数，而论文中使用的轨迹法和风速法均与大气环境遥感监测技术密切相关。

Diskin;Emily M. Gargulinski;Hannah Halliday;Shobha Kondragunta;John B. Nowak;David A. Peterson;Michael A. Robinson;Amber J. Soja;Rebecca A. Washenfelder;Chuanyu Xu;Robert J. Yokelson
title: Age of smoke sampled by aircraft during  FIREX-AQ: methods and critical evaluation
abstract:
Smoke age is an important factor in the chemical and physical evolution of smoke. Two methods for determining the age of smoke are applied to the NASA-NOAA FIREX-AQ field campaign: one based on wind speed and distance, and another using an ensemble of modeled air parcel trajectories. Both methods are evaluated, with the trajectory method, which includes plume rise and uncertainty estimates, proving more accurate. 
 The age of smoke, meaning the time elapsed since it was produced in a fire, is an important parameter for interpreting measurements of evolving smoke composition. This study describes the smoke age estimates developed for large plumes sampled in the 2019 NASA-NOAA FIREX-AQ field experiment. Smoke ages are computed using two methods and applied to observations from two aircraft: the NASA DC-8 and NOAA Chemistry Twin Otter. The first method uses measurements of mean horizontal wind speed, as observed by the sampling aircraft, and distance to the fire to provide a single age estimate for each plume-crossing performed by the aircraft. While this “mean-wind method” uses accurate wind measurements, it can be systematically biased by assumptions that plume rise time is negligible and that winds are homogeneous horizontally and in time during the plume transport. Wind inhomogeneities due to terrain effects and day-to-night transition, among other factors, affected some plumes during FIREX-AQ. The mean-wind method therefore performs best for short-range transport over level terrain with steady winds. The second method relies on upwind air parcel trajectories and plume rise computed with multiple high-resolution meteorological datasets. This “trajectory-based method” quantifies age uncertainty from the meteorological ensemble, plume rise speed, wind speed errors, and fire location. The second method also resolves age differences from the center to edge of a transect. Still, it is susceptible to errors in the meteorological model. With careful comparison of the simulated trajectories to smoke transport observed from geostationary satellite imagery described here, we filter out many trajectory errors and improve the smoke age estimates. Across the two aircraft, the dataset provides ages for over 43 h (815 transects) of in situ measurements in smoke plumes from 115 different fires, with smoke ages ranging from 1 min to 40 h. The two age methods are strongly correlated (R = 0.89) for the periods during FIREX-AQ when both ages are available. The mean-wind age is systematically 12 % younger than the trajectory-based age and the median absolute difference between them is 15 % (21 % for mean). The favorable agreement between the two age methods reflects that the mean-wind method was selectively applied to plumes with little wind variability. Trajectory-based ages are available for more of the FIREX-AQ smoke observations than the mean-wind ages. The median trajectory-based age uncertainty during FIREX-AQ is 24 % and the mean uncertainty is 37 %, due to a long-tailed distribution. The main source of age uncertainty is spread within the meteorological ensemble, followed by discrepancy between measured and modeled wind speed, then other factors like plume rise. The age uncertainty variable enables the user to identify periods with high or low confidence in the age estimate, thereby informing studies of smoke aging. Smoke ages data are available at https://doi.org/10.5067/ASDC/FIREXAQ_MetNav_     AircraftInSitu_DC8_Data_1 (Bennett et al., 2020) for the NASA DC-8 and https://doi.org/10.5067/ASDC/SUBORBITAL/     FIREXAQ_Analysis_N48_Data_1 (Holmes, 2021a) for the NOAA Chemistry Twin Otter.

authors: Shibo Cui;Ni Li;Shiruo Hu;Zhiqi Wan;Jiaru Wang;Jinchao Tang;Ruixi Zhang;Yingjia Li;Xinpeng Yu;Yiqian Tan;Wenbo Shan;Jianshi Zhao
title: CFDID: a China Flood Disaster Impact  Database from 1994 to 2023
abstract:
Floods have caused widespread societal and economic impacts in China, yet long-term and systematic records remain scarce. Using document scanning and large language models, we compiled and manually verified 1716 flood disaster records from 66 official documents covering 1994 to 2023. This open database provides a more complete picture of flood impacts in China than widely used international sources and can support research, disaster preparedness, risk reduction and insurance. 
 China is one of the countries most severely affected by flood disasters. Long-term and systematic flood impact data are essential for flood risk assessment, flood impact model calibration, disaster prevention and reduction. However, an open, long-term, China-focused event-scale database with detailed flood disaster impact indicators remains lacking. Here we present the China Flood Disaster Impact Database (CFDID), which contains 1716 flood disaster event records from 1994 to 2023, including 1391 parent-event (L1) records. CFDID is compiled from 66 official documents and covers five flood-related disaster categories: rainstorm flood, typhoon, snowmelt flood, ice-jam flood, and dam-break flood. Each record includes date, location, disaster category, data source and available values for eight impact indicators: deaths and missing persons, affected population, affected cropland area, damaged cropland area, failed cropland area, collapsed dwellings, damaged dwellings, and direct economic losses. The database was constructed using a workflow that combines optical character recognition (OCR), large language model (LLM)-based information extraction, and manual verification, thereby improving the efficiency of converting unstructured text information into structured event records while ensuring data quality. Relative to the corresponding official national totals during 1994–2023, the impacts reported in L1 records in CFDID account for 68.49 % of deaths and missing persons, 72.24 % of affected population, 60.70 % of affected cropland area, 65.67 % of collapsed dwellings, and 74.86 % of direct economic losses. Compared with commonly used international flood impact databases, CFDID contains more detailed event records and accounts for higher percentages of the corresponding official totals for most impact indicators. CFDID also includes agricultural impact indicators, which are rarely available in international hazard impact databases. CFDID is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22918521 (Cui et al., 2026) and will be continuously updated by year.

authors: Mariana Gomez;Héctor Aguilera;Julian Koch;Willem Jan Zaadnoordijk;Georgina Arnó;Montse Colomer;Benjamin Marchant;Bentje Brauns;Peter van der Keur;Klaus Hinsby;Stefan Broda
title: Analysis-ready European Groundwater Monitoring (EUGM) database
abstract:
Groundwater levels across Europe have long been measured by many different national agencies. We gathered and cleaned decades of these measurements from 27 partners in 24 countries, creating one unified, open dataset of over 15,000 monitoring sites. This resource helps scientists study droughts, long-term water level trends, and build better models to manage Europe's groundwater resources. 
 Reliable pan-European groundwater assessment has long been constrained by fragmented monitoring networks, heterogeneous data formats, and uneven quality-control practices across countries. Within the Geological Service for Europe (GSEU), the groundwater quantity working group addressed this gap by compiling groundwater level (GWL) time series from national and regional geological surveys into the European Groundwater Monitoring (EUGM) database. These GWL time series were harmonized through a standardised workflow that included quality control, resampling to monthly median values, outlier detection, artificial-shift detection, completeness filtering, and gap imputation, resulting in harmonized GWL time series at 15,760 monitoring points. The dataset is complemented by dynamic variables, including precipitation and temperature, and by static variables such as soil properties, lithology, terrain metrics, land cover, population density, and hydrological attributes. In addition, groundwater signatures and Standardised Groundwater Index (SGI) time series were derived from the imputed groundwater records to support the characterization and comparison of groundwater dynamics and anomalies across monitoring points. The dataset is further used to illustrate example applications, including long-term GWL trend analysis and SGI-based cluster classification of temporal GWL dynamics. Together, these data products provide a reproducible basis for groundwater resources assessment, modelling and forecasting across Europe.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术高度相关，因为其研究重点是通过卫星观测数据（特别是热红外波段）来识别和分割飞机尾迹（contrail），这直接涉及空气质量监测和大气成分分析。文中使用了高分辨率卫星数据集（ContrailStruct30）和深度学习模型，以精确地追踪和分类这些高空的薄云，这与遥感技术在环境监测中的应用密切相关。

title: ContrailStruct30: a 30 m three-band thermal-infrared dataset for contrail segmentation
abstract:
Aviation contributes to climate change through high-altitude cloud trails. However, tracking these thin clouds with satellites remains difficult due to a lack of detailed reference data. To solve this, we created a high-resolution satellite dataset to identify individual aircraft trails. Using advanced deep learning models, we showed that these trails can be mapped with precision. This work bridges satellite monitoring and climate research, helping build greener aviation technologies. 
 Aircraft contrails are an important source of aviation's non-CO2 climate effects, and fine-scale satellite observations provide a means of characterizing their spatial structure. Distinguishing narrow, adjacent, and overlapping contrails from complex backgrounds requires reference data with explicit pixel-level annotations. We present ContrailStruct30, a three-band thermal-infrared contrail segmentation dataset derived from Sustainable Development Science Satellite 1 (SDGSAT-1) observations at 30 m nominal sampling. The dataset contains 19,455 patches of 256 × 256 pixels from 819 source-scene entries acquired on 305 dates between August 2022 and September 2024, including 9,023 positive patches and 10,432 deliberately selected difficult negatives. Each sample provides an enhanced RGB image, corresponding three-band source values stored as uint16, and a human-corrected binary mask. Construction began with 300 manually annotated patches identified through ADS-B-assisted searches and continued through four rounds of model-assisted annotation, manual correction, and expert review. Fixed training, validation, and test partitions separate both source scenes and acquisition dates. As an application baseline, we developed a MaxViT–U-Net segmentation model and compared it with three public models under a shared training protocol to evaluate foreground recovery, centerline agreement, and difficult-background discrimination. Across three training seeds, the baseline achieved a mean positive-patch test Dice of 0.8230 ± 0.0056 (mean ± standard deviation), with strong foreground overlap and centerline agreement in the common evaluation. By combining fine-scale thermal-infrared observations, diverse contrail morphologies, expert-reviewed labels, and corresponding image representations, ContrailStruct30 provides a reusable resource for extracting fine contrail structures and developing and evaluating high-resolution segmentation methods. The dataset presented in this study corresponds to Version 3, which is publicly available via Figshare at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.33435496.v3 (Yu et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文研究的是从化石燃料燃烧中排放的CO2、CH4和N2O的月度数据集，这与大气环境遥感技术中的大气成分分析（如温室气体监测）密切相关。虽然论文主要关注排放数据而非遥感技术本身，但其涉及的大气成分和排放监测是遥感技术的重要应用领域。
authors: Hanlin Niu;Jiaying Fu;Miao Huang;Xi Li;Xianhong Meng;Wenping Yuan;Shilong Piao
title: A near-real-time monthly dataset of CO2, CH4, and N2O emissions from fossil fuel combustion
abstract:
Fuel combustion is the largest source of greenhouse gases, but existing datasets either lag by years or cover CO2 only. We present a monthly dataset of CO2, CH4, and N2O emissions from fuel combustion for 153 countries and entities, by sector and fuel, from 1960 to 2025. Emissions for 2024 and 2025 are predicted from monthly activity indicators. The dataset supports carbon budget tracking, Global Stocktake assessment and near-real-time monitoring of sectoral emissions. 
 Fuel-combustion greenhouse gas emissions account for about 67 % of the total anthropogenic emissions, and thus reliable estimates lay the foundation for the Global Stocktake, the evaluation of nationally determined contributions (NDCs), and the quantification of remaining carbon budgets. However, to fully understand the current status of greenhouse gas emissions and to formulate policies for effective control of greenhouse gas emissions, a dataset that provides a comprehensive, up-to-date, and sector-specific record of greenhouse gases is needed. This paper presents a global dataset covering CO2, CH4, and N2O from 1960 to 2025. The dataset reports emissions classified by country, sector, fuel, and gas at monthly resolution, covering emissions from fuel combustion. It covers 153 reporting entities, which consist of 150 individually reported countries, one residual entity covering 48 remaining countries and territories, international aviation, and international shipping. Historical emissions from 1960–2023 are reconstructed using emission factors and statistical data of energy consumption derived from International Energy Agency (IEA) energy activity dataset. For the latest two years without available IEA activity data, we constructed a framework for predicting emissions based on historical emissions data and monthly activity indicators from CEIC. We evaluate six individual prediction methods and their ensembles using historical emissions from 2019 to 2023 and select the best prediction method for each specific country, sector, and gas combination. The best method is applied to estimate annual emissions for 2024–2025. In addition, we distribute the annual emission values to monthly values by using monthly activity patterns. The dataset demonstrates that CO2 and N2O show overall increasing trends with CO2 reaching 37.7 Gt CO2 yr-1 in 2025 and N2O reaching 1,057 kt N2O yr-1 in 2025. In contrast, CH4 reached its peak around 1990 and then declined and remained close to 11 Mt CH4 yr-1. Emissions of all three gases also follow a seasonal pattern with emissions being highest in winter and lowest in summer. For validation purposes, we compare our dataset with existing datasets and find good overall agreement. This dataset supports carbon budget tracking, NDC and Global Stocktake assessment, and near-real-time monitoring of sectoral greenhouse gas emissions.

explanation: 该论文虽然使用了地球观测影像（如Sentinel-2、Landsat和MODIS）进行草地的识别和分类，但其主要关注点在于草地数据集的构建、验证和面积估算，而非大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析或气溶胶反演）。因此，它与大气环境遥感技术的关联性不强。
authors: Myroslava Lesiv;Steffen Fritz;Linda See;Stephen Stehman;Martina Dürauer;Ivelina Georgieva;Maria Schepaschenko;Leandro Parente;Radost Stanimirova;Laerte Guimarães Ferreira;Ana Paula Matos;Vinicius Mesquita;Ichsani Wheeler;Tomislav Hengl;Lindsay Sloat
title: An open global reference dataset for natural and improved grasslands and its application for validation and area estimation
abstract:
This paper presents a global reference dataset of 50,045 locations interpreted for 2020 using multi-source Earth observation imagery. It distinguishes detailed grassland classes and supports map validation and design-based area estimation. Testing a global map showed that improved grasslands are harder to identify than natural ones, and definitions strongly affect results. The data can help improve maps and support sound decisions about grassland protection and management. 
 Grasslands support livestock production, biodiversity, carbon storage and numerous other ecosystem services, yet their global monitoring is constrained by a lack of harmonized reference data that distinguish natural and semi-natural grasslands from cultivated systems. Here we present an openly available global reference dataset for grassland characterization, area estimation and map validation (Lesiv et al., 2026, doi: 10.5281/zenodo.23368916). The dataset comprises 50,045 probability-sampled locations distributed across the global land surface and interpreted for 2020 by trained experts using the Geo-Wiki platform. Interpretation used very-high-resolution satellite imagery, Sentinel-2 imagery and Landsat and MODIS vegetation time series along with historical imagery and geotagged photographs where available. Each location was interpreted at least once, while locations with a higher likelihood of grassland occurrence received two independent annotations. The probability-sampling design supports sample-based estimation of classification accuracy and grassland area within design-based inference. Validation of the 2020 Global Pasture Watch version 1 (GPW v1) product yielded overall accuracies of 73.3 % and 66.8 % (standard errors of 0.2 %) for two definitions of cultivated grasslands (“narrow”, which excluded grazed semi-natural grassland and open woodland and “broad”, which included these classes). Natural/semi-natural grasslands were mapped more accurately than cultivated grasslands under both definitions. Cultivated grasslands showed substantial commission errors under the narrow definition and substantial omission errors under the broad definition, with classification difficulties particularly evident in Africa and Asia. Estimated total grassland area was approximately 3.30 billion ha. Under the narrow definition, the distribution to natural/semi-natural and cultivated grasslands was estimated to be 2.97 and 0.33 billion ha, respectively, compared with 1.89 and 1.41 billion ha under the broad definition. Estimated total grassland area was approximately 3.30 billion ha. The dataset provides a transparent and reusable benchmark for grassland map validation, sample-based area estimation, machine-learning development and assessments of grazing systems and grassland-related environmental change.

title: The marine carbonate system in the northwest European shelf seas: a quality-controlled data product (NWESDAP)
abstract:
NWESDAP (Northwest European Shelf Data Analysis Product) is a quality-controlled data product for the marine carbonate system in the northwest European shelf seas based on in situ samples collected during cruises and at fixed time-series stations from 1975 to 2026. The data product consists of 46,545 datapoints, compiled into a consistent format. The internal consistency of the data product is assessed through a rigorous quality control with uncertainties assigned for each component dataset. 
 Continental shelf seas play an important role in the global carbon cycle. At the interface between the land and deep open ocean, shelf seas are typically highly biologically productive, major sites of organic carbon burial in sediments, and are also highly impacted by human activities. To investigate the marine carbon cycle and its variability through space and time, consistent and quality-controlled data products of marine carbonate system variables, such as the Global Ocean Data Analysis Project (GLODAP), are needed. However, GLODAP focuses on the open ocean, limiting its utility for understanding the marine carbonate system in shelf seas. The northwest European shelf (NWES) seas are of particular interest because of their biogeochemical heterogeneity and expected capacity to absorb, export and bury carbon. Here, we present a new data product for this region called the Northwest European Shelf Data Analysis Product (NWESDAP). NWESDAP includes discrete measurements of marine carbonate system variables (total alkalinity, dissolved inorganic carbon and pH) as well as physical and other biogeochemical variables between 43.6° N and 70° N on the NWES and down to 1,000 m depth. NWESDAP is a compilation of datasets of discrete observations (i.e., laboratory measurements of seawater samples, rather than autonomous sensor measurements) from research cruises and time-series stations from 1975 to 2026. Data from rivers, estuaries and fjords are also included. NWESDAP consists of 46,545 data points (of which 5,221 were in GLODAPv2.2023) from around 500 different expeditions and platforms, merged into a consistent format. Data quality flags corresponding to quantified systematic and random uncertainties have been assigned to each dataset depending on the measurement method used and other available metadata provided. Since GLODAP-style quality control (QC) based on deep ocean cross-over analysis is not possible in the shallow NWES seas (mostly < 200 m), a secondary QC based on variable distributions and relationships has been developed to identify suspected erroneous data points and check for systematic biases in specific datasets, aiming to assess the internal consistency of the entire product with respect to the Global Ocean Acidification Observing Network (GOA-ON) climate and weather quality goals so it can be used to investigate the highly variable marine carbon cycle of the NWES. Of the 46,545 datapoints, 24,822 are of at least weather quality, but the rest has been retained as they can still provide important historical context. The data product and associated metadata are available online at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23555137 (Brandon et al., 2026b). We expect this data compilation to facilitate studies of marine carbonate system variability through space and time across the NWES and support the assessment of carbon stocks and fluxes. NWESDAP will also provide a foundation for evaluating the impact of climate change and anthropogenic activities on the carbonate system as well as for validating regional biogeochemical models.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它涉及未来的卫星重力任务（NGGM和MAGIC），这些任务用于测量地球上的质量运输，这是大气成分分析的一个重要方面。论文还提到了卫星重力产品和数据模拟，这与大气环境遥感技术中的卫星观测和数据分析密切相关。
authors: Marius Schlaak;Julia Pfeffer;Roland Pail;Marie Bouih;Alejandro Blazquez;Benoit Meyssignac;Ilias Daras
title: Simulation database for impact studies of the NGGM and MAGIC gravity missions
abstract:
In this article, we describe the ESA SING dataset. It consists of simulation results for future satellite gravity missions that measure mass transport on Earth. The dataset contains data products that display realistic noise behaviour, as we can expect from current and upcoming satellite missions. It allows users to gain early experience with data products from the next generation of gravity missions and to prepare to take advantage of the improved resolution that will become available. 
 The ESA-SING dataset provides simulated satellite gravity products for three future gravimetry mission constellations: GRACE-C-like, NGGM, and MAGIC. The dataset is developed in the frame of the ESA SING project (www.esa-sing.org) and is based on the ESA Earth System Model 2.0. For the first time, the ESA SING dataset delivers simulated gravity products (L2 & L3) consistently generated over a 12-year period, including a wide range of mass redistribution processes as well as mission-specific errors, arising from instrumental noise and background model errors. In addition to the simulated gravity fields and their residual errors, static empirical variance-covariance matrices for 5-day and 30-day solutions, derived from Monte Carlo simulations, enable the assessment of the expected mission uncertainties. The dataset enables users to assess the impact of future satellite gravimetry missions on applications in hydrology, oceanography, cryosphere, solid-Earth, climate, and geodesy across various temporal and spatial scales. A comparison with uncertainties from the historical GRACE record confirms that the uncertainties of the simulated GRACE-C-like mission are of the same order of magnitude, providing confidence in the validity of the ESA-SING dataset. A global evaluation of the products shows that the NGGM and MAGIC missions will enable high-frequency (sub-weekly) observations together with significantly improved spatial resolution for 30-day and long-term products. However, NGGM-only observations, while comparable to MAGIC in performance, are limited to latitudes between ±70° due to their inclined orbits. To address the polar gap, spherical cap regularisation is applied to NGGM-only solutions, and user recommendations are provided. Overall, the ESA-SING dataset allows users to evaluate mission-specific performance for upcoming satellite gravity missions. Its closed-loop simulations facilitate quantification of expected uncertainties in 5-day and 30-day gravity products, as well as trend and annual-cycle estimates. Moreover, the ESA SING dataset enables users to gain early experience in handling NGGM and MAGIC data and to prepare for the next generation of satellite gravimetry products.

explanation: 该论文主要关注河川流量的谱记忆诊断和降雨-径流模型输出，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）的关系较弱。
authors: Lijian Ren
title: A benchmark dataset of null-calibrated streamflow spectral-memory diagnostics for five CAMELS-family archives, with open rainfall-runoff model outputs for CAMELS-GB v2
abstract:
Rivers carry a memory of the landscape around them, shaping how they respond to new rain. We assembled information from 3,010 river monitoring sites in five public data collections. For each site we measured how long this memory lasts and compared patterns across regions and models. Accounting for memory helped in some regions but not others. The dataset helps researchers test water models more transparently; the memory measure compares rivers, it does not show how water is stored. 
 This article describes a reusable benchmark dataset, rather than a standalone methods paper, of streamflow spectral-memory diagnostics computed from daily discharge records in five CAMELS-family archives (CAMELS-US, CAMELS-GB v2, CAMELS-BR v1.2, CAMELS-AUS v2 and CAMELS-DK; 3,010 gauges in total). For each gauge the release provides the positive-integral autocorrelation time of discharge anomalies, local spectral-slope curves on the raw frequency axis and on the release-defined memory-normalized coordinate De =τacf f, dispersion statistics with gauge- and region-cluster uncertainty, and matched stochastic reference products. For CAMELS-GB v2 it also provides the outputs of three open rainfall-runoff models and two seasonal references under a common chronological split. The De coordinate and the null-calibration ladder are operational fields and reference products defined for this release from standard signal processing and transparent simulations; they are not presented as previously validated, universal techniques. The archive-level characterization is intentionally bounded: memory scaling reduces cross-catchment spectral-curve dispersion in US, GB and BR (24.0 %, 14.7 % and 11.8 %), is weak and uncertain in AUS (7.7 %, region-cluster 95 % interval -0.7–27.6 %), and shows no reduction in the lowland DK archive (-4.7 %, -20.2–11.1 %). The matched references quantify how much alignment can arise from serial correlation alone. A CAMELS-GB worked reuse case, based on three independent models and 544 gauges (308 disagreement gauges), does not support spectral distance as a universal model-selection rule (median decision delta +0.124, bootstrap 95 % CI +0.085 to +0.163). The release is intended for catchment-scale spectral characterization, frequency-specific model comparison and reproducible benchmark construction; it does not establish a storage mechanism or a cross-archive ranking rule. The curated dataset is available from Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22055294 (Ren, 2026).

explanation: 该论文主要关注的是地质历史时期的海洋温度记录和年代框架，涉及的是古气候学和环境科学领域，而非大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测或大气成分分析。
