title: The MioOcean Age Framework: Age Model Database and Chronoinformatics Approach for synchronised Miocene Ocean Temperature, Climate and Proxy Records
abstract:
Reliable climate histories depend on knowing when changes occurred. We critically evaluated and harmonised the age information underlying global Miocene ocean temperature records, creating a consistent age framework, an open and updateable database, and a new approach for assessing chronological reliability. Our Chronoinformatics approach provides a transferable way to organise, evaluate and update age information for future climate syntheses. 
 Understanding climate evolution depends fundamentally on time: when changes occurred, how rapidly they occurred, and whether changes recorded at geographically disparate locations were synchronous. Palaeoclimate syntheses, which can provide important evidence for broader climate assessments, such as the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Assessment Reports, require chronological frameworks that are sufficiently accurate and comparable between records across both Milankovitch and longer geological timescales. The Miocene Ocean Temperature Synthesis (MioOcean) provides an important test case, compiling upper ocean and bottom water temperature records spanning 23.04–5.333 million years ago. Within MioOcean, the MioOcean Age Model Group (MioAGE) evaluates and harmonises the depth and age models underlying these temperature records and develops a consistent chronological framework for reconstructing and interpreting the evolution of Miocene ocean temperatures across space and time. Here, we present the MioOcean Chronoinformatics approach applied to 69 sites, from which 38 key sites were synchronised into the MioOcean Age Framework through detailed chronological evaluation and harmonisation of the age models using biostratigraphy, magnetostratigraphy, and/or astrochronology. We critically assess published depth and age models, then verify, standardise and, where needed, revise the chronologies within a consistent framework anchored to the Geologic Time Scale 2012. These 38 sites comprise 53 individual age models, all of which required verification and standardisation, with 33 additionally requiring revision. The resulting chronologies are integrated into the open, machine-readable and updateable MioOcean Age Model Database, which preserves depth and age models, chronological tie points, metadata and provenance. Across 10,560 Miocene temperature data points, synchronisation resulted in a mean age change of 28 kyr, demonstrating changes that are important on Milankovitch timescales (18–405 kyr), while the largest offsets reach several million years (up to 7.121 Myr) and can alter the geological interval to which individual proxy observations are assigned. We also present the MioAGE Reliability Grid across all key sites to evaluate differences in Age Model Quality and Reporting Quality among the major chronological approaches, and integrate these into site-level assessments. Together, these developments establish a consistent and reproducible chronological foundation for MioOcean and demonstrate the utmost importance of preserving the underlying sample, depth and chronological information required to reproduce and update palaeoclimate records. More broadly, we introduce Chronoinformatics, an approach for systematically organising, interrogating, evaluating, preserving and updating chronological information that is now available for use across geological intervals, proxy systems and large-scale community syntheses, ultimately feeding into IPCC’s Assessment Reports. The MioOcean age compilation is hosted on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22258616; Drury, Tangunan et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它涉及使用被动微波卫星任务（AMSR2和SMAP）融合数据来创建亚日土壤湿度数据集（MSM4D），以支持快速湿化和干化等短期地表过程研究，这与空气质量监测、卫星观测和大气成分分析等领域相关。
authors: Mengran Wang;Peilin Song;Tianjie Zhao;Yongqiang Zhang;Haigen Zhao
title: MSM4D: a sub-daily soil moisture dataset with four nominal overpass slots from AMSR2-SMAP fusion (2015–2024)
abstract:
Soil moisture can change within hours after rainfall, but most satellite products observe it only once or twice a day. We created a global 36 km soil moisture dataset for 2015–2024 by combining observations from two microwave satellite missions into four daily observation slots. The dataset greatly increases the number of days with multiple observations while remaining consistent with ground measurements, supporting studies of rapid wetting, drying, and other short-term land-surface processes. 
 Soil moisture (SM) is an essential variable for hydrological processes, agricultural monitoring, drought and flood assessment, and land–atmosphere interactions. Existing passive microwave SM products provide global observations but are generally limited to daily or twice-daily sampling, leaving rapid intraday wetting and drying processes insufficiently sampled. In this study, we developed the “Multi-source Sub-daily Soil Moisture dataset with four daily nominal overpass slots (MSM4D)”, a 36 km sub-daily SM dataset that integrates Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR2)-derived estimates and Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) observations from 2015 to 2024. MSM4D provides four nominal overpass slots, including TAMSR2-D, TSMAP-D, TAMSR2-A, and TSMAP-A, together with a daily-mean product on the Equal-Area Scalable Earth Grid 2.0. A ten-day-scale training strategy establishes grid-wise relationships between AMSR2 microwave observations and SMAP Level-3 (L3) SM retrievals, enabling SMAP-consistent SM estimates for the two AMSR2-derived temporal slots. By adding these temporally complementary estimates to the two SMAP-based slots, the global mean proportion of days with at least two valid observations increased from 21.31 % for SMAP alone to 71.78 % for MSM4D. Across the core validation grids, MSM4D achieved an overall unbiased root mean square error (ubRMSE) of 0.048 cm³ cm⁻³, with the AMSR2-derived slots showing accuracy comparable to the SMAP-based slots. Validation across additional sites further supported the robustness of the dataset over diverse land-surface conditions. Event-based analyses further showed that the enhanced temporal sampling provides additional information on intraday wetting and drydown processes that may be obscured by daily aggregation, smoothed in model-based products such as SMAP Level-4 (L4), or insufficiently sampled by twice-daily observations. MSM4D therefore provides a decade-long, observation-constrained data record for investigating sub-daily SM variability and associated hydrological processes. The dataset is available at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.34700667 (Song and Wang, 2026).

explanation: 该论文研究使用POLDER-3和DPC-2卫星的多角度、多光谱和偏振观测数据，构建了双向偏振分布函数（BPDF）数据库，并开发了统一的大气校正框架。这些技术涉及大气成分分析、卫星观测和空气质量监测，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Zhe Ji;Zhengqiang Li;Gerrit de Leeuw;Cheng Chen;Yahui Che;Zihan Zhang;Luo Zhang
title: A BPDF database retrieved using multi-angle, multispectral and polarimetric observations from POLDER-3 and DPC-2
abstract:
Earlier databases ignore the effects of atmospheric particles on polarized land signals. Using ground data and modelling, we processed two missions and built two databases. Ignoring particles changed the surface signal by over 10 % in 60–75 % of observations. Records corresponded under similar conditions nearly a decade apart. Coarser observations showed stronger land-dependent links between surface mixing and the signal. The method supports long-term records and atmospheric particle estimates. 
 The bidirectional polarization distribution function (BPDF) characterizes the dependence of land-surface polarized reflectance on illumination and viewing geometry and provides a key surface boundary condition for polarimetric retrievals of aerosol properties. In recent years, the increasing number of polarimeters in orbit has stimulated growing interest in polarized surface reflectance. Reliable multisensor BPDF databases are therefore urgently needed. However, deriving surface polarized reflectance that is comparable across spectral bands and sensors remains challenging. Earlier databases generally corrected only for molecular scattering and adopted the 865 nm results as the final surface polarized reflectance, assuming that aerosol effects were negligible under low aerosol loading and that a single band adequately represented surface polarization. This approach neither explicitly accounted for aerosol effects nor exploited the weak spectral dependence of land-surface polarized reflectance. In fact, even under low-aerosol-loading conditions, across the POLDER-3 and DPC-2 observations used in this study, the relative differences between surface polarized reflectance obtained using molecular-only correction and that obtained by accounting for both molecular and aerosol effects exceeded 10 % in approximately 60 %–75 % of the observations at 490, 670 and 865 nm. Moreover, global BPDF studies have relied primarily on POLDER observations. Because most existing studies use observations from 2005–2013, their results may not adequately represent current land-surface conditions. Newly operational polarimeters therefore require an atmospheric-correction method applicable across-sensors to update existing BPDF records and support future BPDF studies. In addition, the effects of mixing among different surface types on BPDF remain poorly understood. Here, we developed a unified atmospheric-correction framework that uses Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) aerosol optical depth and vector radiative transfer calculations together with vector radiative-transfer calculations to account for the effects of both atmospheric molecules and aerosols. After correcting the multiband observations, the spectral consistency of the multiband surface polarized reflectance was substantially improved. On this basis, we used weighted fusion to derive a common estimate of surface polarized reflectance from the three corrected bands. The framework was applied to POLDER-3 observations from 2005–2013 and DPC-2 observations from 2022–2023, producing two quality-flagged BPDF databases. The database is publicly available and registered at doi.org/10.57760/sciencedb.015ek. For the cross-sensor evaluation, directional observations acquired under similar surface and observation conditions were matched between the two sensors. The matched directional observations yielded correlation coefficients of 0.60 to 0.87 across 12 International Geosphere–Biosphere Programme (IGBP) land-cover classes, showing clear positive correspondence under similar surface and observation conditions despite the nearly decade-long separation between the two sensor records. The subpixel analysis further showed that the higher-resolution DPC-2 observation sequences were generally more homogeneous, with a mean dominant land-cover fraction 5.8 percentage points higher than that of POLDER-3. After accounting for observation geometry, a lower dominant land-cover fraction was associated with lower surface polarized reflectance, with a greater decrease for POLDER-3 than for DPC-2, indicating a stronger association between surface polarized reflectance and subpixel composition at coarser spatial resolution. The direction of this relationship varied among land-cover classes, showing that subpixel mixing does not produce a uniform monotonic shift but also depends on the polarization contrast between dominant and secondary surface components. By developing a unified atmospheric-correction framework, this study extends BPDF database construction from single-band and single-sensor processing to multiband and multisensor applications. The resulting framework provides a foundation for updating historical BPDF records, developing long-term multisensor records of land-surface polarized reflectance, and improving the surface boundary conditions used in atmospheric polarimetric retrievals.

explanation: 该论文主要研究海底山脉（seamounts）的探测和目录编制，利用重力异常和海底地形数据进行分析。虽然涉及卫星测量和地球物理技术，但与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）关系不大，因此相关性较低。
authors: Yi Gao;Jinyun Guo;Shaoshuai Ya;Daocheng Yu;Xin Liu;Cheinway Hwang
title: SDUST2026SM: a global seamount catalog based on vertical gradient of gravity anomaly and bathymetric data
abstract:
Satellites can reveal underwater mountains where ship surveys are sparse. We combined satellite measurements of Earth's gravity with maps of seafloor depth to compile a global catalog of 67,374 seamounts checked by visual inspection. This is 55 % more than in a widely used 2023 catalog, especially for smaller features. The open dataset can help researchers study seafloor geology and plan future ocean-mapping surveys, though some small and deep seamounts remain undetected. 
 This study applies the integrated seamount detection and height estimation method based on vertical gradient of gravity anomaly (VGGA) and bathymetry (ISDHEB) to detect and catalog seamounts across the global ocean between 80° N and 80° S. This analysis uses the SWOT_04 VGGA field released by the Scripps Institution of Oceanography (SIO) and the GEBCO_2025 bathymetry grid. The global ocean was divided into 10° × 10° processing tiles, each surrounded by a 1° overlapping buffer. Candidate features were screened using multiple constraints, including local maxima, closed contours, area and amplitude, circular or elliptical fitting, Jaccard similarity, and seamount exclusion zones. Marker-controlled watershed segmentation was used to separate multi-peak anomalies. Foot-of-slope points were then identified from the slope and second derivative of bathymetric profiles to estimate base depth and seamount height, followed by visual quality control. A total of 68,934 candidate seamounts at least 100 m high were identified. Small, medium, and large seamounts accounted for 67.6 %, 30.9 %, and 1.5 % of the candidates, respectively. After visual inspection, 67,374 targets were retained in the high-confidence seamount set, corresponding to an overall candidate acceptance rate of 97.74 %. The high-confidence catalog contains 55.0 % more seamounts than the SIO 2023 catalog, with most additional targets having heights below 1 km. The cumulative height-frequency relationship follows a clear power law above 0.8 km but progressively deviates at lower heights. The expanded catalog reflects the combined benefits of SWOT-enhanced gravity information, updated bathymetry, and the integrated detection and height-estimation procedure. The resulting catalog provides a basis for studies of seafloor tectonics, shipborne bathymetric survey planning, and marine ecological and resource investigations. The SDUST2026SM dataset is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23277209 (Gao et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文研究的是利用雷达风廓线仪（radar wind profiler）获取中国低层垂直风切变（low-level vertical wind shear）数据，分析风雨关系，以提高短期降雨预报能力。这与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，尤其是与空气质量监测、大气成分分析、卫星观测等领域相关，因为风切变是影响大气污染物扩散和降水形成的重要因素。

authors: Ning Li;Yongguang Zheng;Hui Xu;Tianmeng Chen;Xiaoran Guo;Linxi Zhao;Yuping Sun;Xuewei Cai;Honglong Yang;Liping Zeng;Jianping Guo
title: A high-resolution dataset of pre-rainfall low-level vertical wind shear derived from radar wind profilers across China
abstract:
To better understand how winds change before rainfall, we created a unique dataset from 28 radar wind profiler stations across China. It captures wind shear every six minutes during the two hours before rainfall. Stronger rainfall is preceded by a rapid increase and vertical shift in shear, while lighter rainfall shows steadier conditions. The data reveal changes missed by widely used weather analyses and may help improve short-term rainfall forecasts. 
 Favorable low-level vertical wind shear (VWS) is an important dynamic feature conducive to rainfall development. However, continuous observations capable of resolving the fine-scale vertical structure and rapid pre-rainfall evolution of VWS remain limited. To address this observational gap, we developed a high-resolution low-level VWS dataset from wind measurements collected by a network of 28 radar wind profiler (RWP) stations across China during 2023–2025, with a focus on the 2 h preceding rainfall onset. The dataset provides bulk VWS for both the fixed 0.6–3.0 km layer and arbitrary combinations of vertical levels, local layer VWS, layer-mean VWS, maximum VWS, and the altitude of maximum VWS, with a temporal resolution of 6 min and a vertical resolution of 120 m over 0.6–4.08 km AGL. Comparison with collocated radiosonde measurements supports the reliability of the RWP-derived VWS, while comparison with ERA5 shows that the reanalysis underestimates localized maximum VWS and does not reproduce its rapid minute-scale evolution. Non-HR events are generally associated with stronger but relatively steady background VWS, whereas HR events show a pronounced nonlinear increase in local low-level VWS during approximately the final 30 min before rainfall onset. The latter is accompanied by an upward shift in the altitude of maximum VWS, indicating a redistribution of the strongest shear within the lower troposphere. These contrasting evolution patterns demonstrate the ability of the dataset to resolve transient and vertically localized changes in pre-rainfall dynamic environments that are not adequately represented by coarser-resolution reanalysis data. The dataset is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23432237 (Li and Guo, 2026), which can serve as a valuable benchmark for diagnosing pre-rainfall dynamic environments to advance regional HR nowcasting. Accordingly, to realize such forecasting improvements, we must leverage fine-scale dynamic structures derived from RWP measurements for more complete characterizations of prestorm environments.

authors: Rajesh Kumar;Claudio Sanchez;Juan Manuel Castillo;Jian-Guo Li;Bijoy Thompson;Pratiman Patel;Alvin Ng;Kaushik Sasmal;Kalli Furtado;Hailin Yan;Liu Jianyu;Hugh Zhang
title: cSINGV v1.0: development and evaluation of a 1.5 km  coupled atmosphere–ocean–wave modelling  system for the Western Maritime Continent
abstract:
Weather over Southeast Asia is shaped by complex interactions between the air, ocean, and waves. We developed a high-resolution model that links these processes to better understand and predict rainfall patterns in the region. The results show that ocean–atmosphere interactions improve the representation and prediction of squall events that affect daily life in Singapore and surrounding regions. This work supports more accurate weather forecasting in the region. 
 This study presents cSINGV v1.0, a high-resolution (1.5 km) regional coupled atmosphere–ocean–wave modelling system developed for the Western Maritime Continent (WMC), a region characterised by complex coastlines, shallow seas, and strong air–sea interactions. The system integrates a convection-permitting atmospheric model (SINGV) with newly configured ocean (NEMO) and wave (WAVEWATCH III) components within a unified coupling framework based on the Regional Coupled Suite and OASIS3-MCT coupler. Its primary contribution is the development of a fully coupled system that enables two-way interactions between atmosphere, ocean, and waves at kilometre scale. Before coupling, the ocean and wave components are configured in standalone mode for the WMC.The model is evaluated using a six-month simulation (January–June 2019) against multiple observational and reanalysis datasets. The ocean and wave components show good agreement with reference datasets, with sea surface temperature errors generally below 0.5 °C and significant wave height errors around 0.2 m. This agreement is maintained in the fully coupled configuration. The influence of coupling is assessed by comparing the coupled and uncoupled atmospheric configurations. Results show that coupling improves the spatial organisation of precipitation, the diurnal cycle over the ocean, and the offshore propagation of convection, while differences in near-surface atmospheric variables remain modest. Process-based analysis indicates that these improvements are primarily linked to enhanced latent heat flux driven by thermodynamic air–sea feedbacks associated with sea surface temperature variability. Case studies of individual Sumatra squall events further suggest that coupling may influence the organisation and persistence of eastward-propagating convection. The magnitude of this influence appears to depend on the dominant convective regime, although a larger sample of events is needed to confirm this dependence. Overall, cSINGV provides a physically consistent framework for representing coupled processes in the WMC and a useful platform for investigating air–sea–wave interactions at convection-permitting scales.

authors: Qitao Cui;Li Dong;Bin Wang
title: A deep-atmosphere extension in a nonhydrostatic dynamical core: formulation and idealized tests
abstract:
Many atmospheric models use shallow approximation that work well when the model top is low. As models top now reach higher layers, these approximation need to be relaxed. We develop a deep atmosphere dynamical core(GMCORE), including full deep atmosphere dynamics, and spherical geometry. The tests case with idealized baroclinic waves and tropical cyclones show that the new model reproduces known results and can alter storm trajectory, suggesting value for future high-top and tropical studies. 
 We have developed a deep-atmosphere extension within the GMCORE (Grid-Model dynamical CORE) using a dry terrain-following mass-based coordinate. The new dycore retains the full three-dimensional Coriolis force, accounts for the height dependence of gravity, and introduces radial metric corrections into the discrete operators, while preserving the main structure of the original solver. Numerical consistency is examined through convergence and balanced-state stability tests. Two idealized test cases are used for evaluation: a baroclinic wave test and a tropical cyclone test. In the standard Earth-radius baroclinic wave experiment, the deep- and shallow-atmosphere solutions are similar, whereas in the reduced-radius X20 experiment the GMCORE deep-atmosphere dycore reproduces the clear separation reported in earlier studies. In the tropical-cyclone experiment, the deep-atmosphere formulation has little effect on storm intensity and warm-core structure, but leads to a systematic south-westward trajectory shift relative to the shallow-atmosphere simulation. The trajectory difference is linked to an organised inner asymmetry. This includes a dipole-like pattern connected to  2Ωcosφ∂w∂y and a low-level easterly anomaly. These results support the numerical consistency of the GMCORE deep-atmosphere implementation and suggest that nontraditional Coriolis effects can influence low-latitude vortex motion, although a complete dynamical attribution requires further diagnosis.

authors: Mohammad Sabah;Mauro Cacace;Inga Berre;Iman R. Kivi;Hannes Hofmann
title: Hybrid implicit–explicit XFEM simulation of injection-induced seismicity: resolving multi-scale rupture nucleation and dynamics
abstract:
Injecting fluids underground for energy projects can trigger earthquakes. Predicting these events is difficult because underground pressure changes slowly, while faults can move in a fraction of a second. We developed a computer method that switches between two ways of calculating these processes. In our test, it reduced computing time by 62 % while giving similar estimates of earthquake size and total fault movement. Differences in the fastest movements show that further testing is needed. 
 This study presents a novel hybrid implicit–explicit time-integration strategy for simulating injection-induced fault reactivation within a fully coupled poroelastodynamic extended finite element (XFEM) framework. Modeling these systems is inherently challenging due to the extreme separation of temporal scales – ranging from hours to days for fluid diffusion to milliseconds for dynamic rupture. Although the fully implicit formulation can provide enhanced numerical stability, stability alone does not guarantee sufficient temporal accuracy during nonlinear fault rupture. The results demonstrate close agreement between simulations with minimum time-step sizes of 10−5 and 10−6 s for the investigated slip and event-scale observables on the adopted spatial mesh, indicating temporal convergence for these quantities at 10−5 s. This time-step size is substantially smaller than the mesh-based explicit stability estimate. To reduce computational cost, the proposed strategy employs an implicit solver for quasi-static loading and nucleation and switches to a central-difference-based mechanical solver with implicit pressure integration once a prescribed slip-velocity threshold is exceeded. At a switching threshold of 0.01 m s−1, the hybrid simulation requires approximately 10.0 h, compared with 26.4 h for the fully implicit reference, corresponding to a computational-time reduction of 62.12 %. The hybrid strategy reproduces the overall rupture sequence, stress evolution, final accumulated fault slip, and seismic moment. However, differences remain in the timing and magnitude of peak slip velocities, rupture-propagation speeds, and transient particle motion. These findings demonstrate the computational potential of the hybrid formulation for the investigated two-dimensional configuration, while highlighting the need for further assessment of transient dynamic accuracy and computational performance across different spatial discretizations and geological conditions.

title: Slope-Constrained Orography (SCO v1.0) for explicit discrete-slope control in terrain preprocessing: a case study with WRF-ARW (v4.6.1)
abstract:
High-resolution weather models over mountains need terrain smoothing to avoid crashing, but standard methods smooth everywhere regardless of need. We developed Slope-Constrained Orography, a tool that uses one slope-angle setting to adjust only the points that are too steep. Tested over the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, stable simulations were achieved while modifying far less terrain than standard smoothing, offering a simpler approach to running weather models over steep terrain. 
 Kilometre-scale Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) simulations over terrain with steep slopes often require strong smoothing to prevent numerical instability, but conventional domain-wide filters alter terrain at every grid point, regardless of whether local slopes require reduction. Slope-Constrained Orography (SCO) is an offline terrain preprocessing method that prescribes a target slope angle θ and adjusts only those grid points whose eight-neighbour elevation differences exceed the implied bound, leaving the remaining terrain unchanged. By prescribing the slope constraint directly, SCO provides a geometrically interpretable primary user-facing parameter for terrain construction and stability testing. In a 1 km WRF case over the highly complex terrain of the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, the least-modified stable SCO member among those tested modifies 14 % of points with a mean elevation change of 8.2 m, compared with 100 % modification and 108.1 m for the corresponding WRF Preprocessing System (WPS) member. The successful SCO configuration produces lower near-surface wind and temperature errors in this case.

authors: Bernard Aumont;Richard Valorso;Andrew Rickard;Mike Jenkin;Julia Lee-Taylor;John Orlando;Sasha Madronich;Luc Vereecken;Marie Camredon
title: GECKO-A v1.0: exploring VOC oxidation trajectories through comparison with the master chemical mechanism
abstract:
This study presents the first open-source release of a tool that automatically generates chemical mechanisms for the atmospheric oxidation of organic compounds. Simulations for five hydrocarbons, under conditions ranging from urban to remote, are compared with a benchmark mechanism. Results show that describing successive oxidation steps is key to simulating the formation of low-volatility and water-soluble species important for aerosols. A reduced mechanism reproduces most of these results. 
 Numerical models are crucial tools for understanding complex chemical systems such as the atmosphere, and their sensitivity across a range of conditions. In atmospheric chemistry models, reaction mechanisms are used to represent chemical transformations and define the underlying system of equations. Building highly explicit mechanisms that capture the full complexity of organic oxidation occurring in the atmosphere remains challenging owing to the large number of intermediates involved, the breadth of reaction pathways, and the limited availability of reliable kinetic and thermodynamic data. The Generator for Explicit Chemistry and Kinetics of Organics in the Atmosphere (GECKO-A) was developed to address these limitations by enabling the systematic construction of near-explicit mechanisms. Here, we present its first open-source release (v1.0), which incorporates updated chemical protocols and structure-activity relationships, together with its companion box model for mechanism integration. GECKO-A's performance is benchmarked through systematic comparisons with the Master Chemical Mechanism (MCM v3.3.1), based on simulations of the oxidation of five representative hydrocarbons (butane, octane, dodecane, toluene, and α-pinene) under environmental conditions ranging from urban to remote. The two approaches yield similar oxidation pathways for small and structurally simple compounds. However, differences increase with the size and complexity of the carbon backbone. In particular, the simplifications inherent to the MCM tend to limit the formation of multifunctional products and promote earlier fragmentation, resulting in notable discrepancies in the predicted volatility of secondary organic carbon and, consequently, in secondary organic aerosol yields. These discrepancies stem from how each mechanism treats multigenerational oxidation. The two approaches remain similar for early-generation products, but diverge as later generations become predominant. This divergence also extends to the water solubility of secondary organic carbon, and to its partitioning into aqueous condensed phases. GECKO-A also enables mechanism generation at different levels of chemical resolution. A reduced mechanism, denoted red-GECKO-A, is compared to the high-resolution mechanism used throughout this study. It closely reproduces the simulated oxidative trajectories for most parent compounds and scenarios. Discrepancies emerge for octane and dodecane under NOx-poor conditions.

title: The Role of Turbulence in Ice Microphysics and Sedimentation in Arctic Mixed‐Phase Clouds: Evidence From Yearlong Observations
abstract: Despite the recognized importance of turbulence in Arctic mixed‐phase cloud (AMPC) persistence, its effects on ice microphysics and size‐dependent sedimentation remain poorly understood. Using yearlong shipborne MOSAiC observations, we examine these processes across eddy dissipation rate (EDR) ranges. The mixed‐phase layer base (MLB) shows relatively high EDR, with the highest range (10−3.5–10−2 m2 s−3) associated with lower temperatures (TMLB). At the MLB, the typical relationship between particle size and ice sedimentation weakens as EDR increases. Under stronger turbulence, sedimentation is enhanced for layers with smaller particles but weakened for those with larger particles, a contrast broadly consistent with preferential sweeping and loitering. These sedimentation changes are accompanied by smaller ice particles in the less cold regime (TMLB > −20°C) and higher ice particle concentrations in the colder regime (TMLB < −20°C). Such sedimentation changes may influence AMPC microphysics and potentially contribute to ice‐recycling processes.

title: Shallow Slip Deficit: An Intrinsic Property of Continental Earthquakes, Slightly Enhanced by Fault Maturity
abstract: A depletion of earthquake slip in the shallow crust (shallow coseismic slip deficit, or coseismic SSD) has been observed on <30, Mw ≥ 6 continental earthquakes, and attributed to the immaturity of the ruptured faults. We question the factors that contribute to the coseismic SSD. We built the largest earthquake source model database available to date, with 1078 models providing coseismic SSD estimates on 163 Mw ≥ 6, various slip mode, continental earthquakes worldwide since 1990. We also built a database providing their fault maturity parameters (initiation age, net displacement, length, slip rate). Our combined earthquake‐fault analysis reveals that coseismic SSD of continental earthquakes, whatever their slip mode, is primarily controlled by the relation between their magnitude and peak slip depth, and, to a much lesser extent, by the fault maturity. A model where earthquake slip produces zero stress drop on the shallow velocity strengthening fault section reproduces the data well.

title: Detecting the Oceanic Moho Using Teleseismic P‐Wave Coda Autocorrelations of Ocean Bottom Seismograph Records
abstract: Although active‐source seismic methods can image the oceanic Mohorovičić discontinuity (Moho) at high resolution, their high cost motivates passive approaches using OBS, for which receiver functions (RF) are often complicated by instrument tilt, azimuthal misalignment, sedimentary layers, and water‐column reverberations. Here we apply teleseismic P‐wave coda autocorrelation to hydrophone data from OBS to image the oceanic Moho. Compared with vertical‐component data, hydrophone data provide a simpler interpretation because they avoid P‐to‐S conversions and are dominated by reflected and transmitted P‐wave energy. By analyzing autocorrelation results from 22 long‐period and 24 short‐period stations in the NoMelt experiment, we identify a Moho reflection with a TwTT of ∼2.56 s and resolve lateral variations in crustal TwTT that are smoothed out in the radially averaged representations of global velocity models. Combined with previous studies and model tests, this longer‐than‐expected crustal TwTT suggests that a crust‐mantle transition zone may exist beneath the NoMelt region.

title: Intense Magnetopause Erosion at Earth During the May 2024 Solar Storm
abstract: Earth's main magnetic field forms the magnetosphere, shielding the planet from solar wind plasma. Southward interplanetary magnetic fields erode the magnetosphere, a process known as magnetopause erosion, allowing solar wind penetration close to the Earth. While magnetic reconnection is considered a key driver, the mechanism during super geomagnetic storms remains unclear due to limited in situ observations. Here, we report a magnetopause crossing by Arase at 4.96 RE during the May 2024 superstorm, one of the innermost magnetopause crossings ever detected by magnetospheric spacecraft. We observe an anomalous and global reduction in magnetic field intensity extending from the inner magnetosphere to the magnetopause, suggesting global weakening by magnetospheric currents. This weakened magnetic field is responsible for the enhanced magnetopause erosion.

title: Temporal Scaling of Hydrological Signals Reveals Forcing Persistence and Watershed Filtering Across the Contiguous U.S.
abstract: Streamflow temporal persistence reflects both hydrological inputs and watershed filtering, but their relative contributions remain difficult to distinguish. We analyzed spectral scaling in precipitation, evapotranspiration, effective precipitation, streamflow, and the effective precipitation‐to‐streamflow transfer function across 671 contiguous U.S. watersheds. Streamflow and transfer‐function scaling exponents vary more widely across watersheds than those of the hydrological inputs. Combining effective‐precipitation and transfer‐function exponents identifies three regimes: rapid‐response watersheds with weak input persistence and filtering, widespread across the central and eastern U.S.; forcing‐persistent watersheds with persistent inputs but limited filtering, mainly in the West; and hydrologically buffered watersheds with strong filtering, concentrated in the western mountains, northern regions and Southeast. Western mountain buffered watersheds have greater snow influence and baseflow contributions, whereas southeastern buffered watersheds have little snow but more permeable soils and subsurface materials. The two exponents distinguish input persistence from watershed filtering in shaping streamflow persistence.

title: Large‐Scale Coherent Southward Displacement of the Indochina Block: Constraints From New Late Cretaceous Paleomagnetic Studies
abstract: To better constrain the post‐collisional southward displacement of the Indochina Block (ICB) and the crustal deformation of the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, we present a reliable paleomagnetic study of Upper Cretaceous Nanxin Formation redbeds exposed in the Lanping area, at the northern edge of the Lanping‐Simao Terrane (LST). The tilt‐corrected site‐mean direction derived from 30 sites is Ds = 39.3°, Is = 48.4° with α95 = 4.3°, corresponding to a paleomagnetic pole at 55.3°N, 175.5°E with dp/dm = 3.7°/5.6° and a paleolatitude of 29.4°N ± 3.7°N for the sampling area (26.6°N, 99.4°E). This paleomagnetic data set passes both positive fold and reversal tests at 95% and 99% confidence levels. Comparison with the Late Cretaceous pole of the South China Block and the East Asia apparent polar wander path shows that the entire ICB underwent a coherent southward displacement of ∼900 km between the Late Cretaceous and Late Eocene.

authors: James Stinecipher;Stephen A. Montzka;James W. Hannigan;Emmanuel Mahieu;Kevin Bowman;Le Kuai;J. Elliott Campbell
title: Recent Decline in Global Atmospheric COS Driven by Reduced Anthropogenic CS2 Emissions
abstract: Carbonyl sulfide (COS) is an atmospheric tracer for carbon cycle processes. Global observations reveal a rapid decline in COS concentrations beginning in 2016, but the cause of this decline is unknown. Here we show that this decrease is unexpected. Previous COS trends followed rayon production which emits CS2, a COS precursor. However, the recent COS decline coincides with increasing rayon output. Multiple independent observing systems, including NOAA's global flask network and NDACC FTIR retrievals, show a consistent tropospheric COS trend of −1.2 ± 0.1% yr−1 from 2016 to 2022, even as rayon manufacturing increased by 4.1 ± 1.3% yr−1. Using atmospheric models, we demonstrate that the COS decline is consistent with a 2.5% yr−1 reduction in emissions, driven by decreasing CS2 emission factors. Variations in other sources and sinks are unable to account for this trend. These results highlight the need for improved anthropogenic inventories and point toward robust COS applications to the carbon‐cycle through regional analyses.

title: Recent Slowing Arctic‐Amplified Warming Drives an Unprecedented Water Recovery in the World's Most Voluminous Freshwater Lake
abstract: The Lake Baikal, containing one‐fifth of Earth's unfrozen surface freshwater, faces increasing hydrological uncertainty under climate change. Its water balance depends on Selenga River inflow and Angara River outflow. We present a 343‐year combined Selenga and Angara streamflow reconstruction using a tree‐ring network to provide a multi‐century hydroclimatic baseline. The reconstruction captures intermittent drying trends throughout the 20th century, including a ∼90% streamflow decline from high levels, consistent with long‐term regional aridification. This trend has reversed sharply over the last decade showing a most sustained ∼80% increase. The recent hydrological recovery is consistent with basin‐wide vegetation greening, rising lake levels, and favorable eco‐climatic conditions, primarily improved water availability. Rapidly changing atmospheric circulations associated with a regional slowing Arctic‐amplified warming drive enhanced moisture transports. The contrasting trend between recent recovery and preceding long‐term decline underscores the need for adaptive management strategies to account for non‐stationary dynamics in safeguarding critical freshwater resources.

authors: Constance Hjort;Ole B. Andersen;Bjarke Nilsson
title: Iceberg‐Generated Waves From SWOT: Disintegration of Iceberg A‐76A in the Southern Ocean
abstract: Amid rising global temperatures, icebergs are calving more often and drifting into open waters. Their disintegration processes can trigger energetic surface gravity waves that propagate away from the iceberg remain poorly documented. This study presents an analysis of 12 iceberg‐generated wave fields associated with the disintegration of iceberg A‐76A, utilizing sea surface height anomaly data from the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission. We analyzed wave height, wavelength, depth regime, and Time Since Impact (TSI) using wavelet scalograms matched to dispersion curves. Waves fell within the linear intermediate‐to‐deep‐water regime, aligning with findings from Heller et al. (2019, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598‐018‐36634‐3). Correlation found between steepness and TSI, as expected from theory. Preliminary results suggest the potential to infer calving mechanisms and direction from the scalograms. Despite SWOT's limited temporal resolution, demonstrates its unique ability to detect iceberg‐generated and novel view iceberg–ocean interactions, supporting future research with enhanced data and processing capabilities.

explanation: 该论文研究了中国东部结冰云层中过冷液态水和过冷大液滴的特性，并提出了基于多矩微物理方案的数值模拟和预测算法。虽然论文主要关注飞机结冰现象，但其涉及的大气成分分析（如过冷液态水和液滴特性）与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量和云层观测密切相关，因此与该领域具有较强的相关性。
authors: Liping Luo;Hongyang Wang;Ming Xue;Xi Chen;Jing Sun;Rong Zhang
title: Aircraft Icing: In‐Cloud Measurements and Explicit Prediction of Supercooled Large Droplets in Icing Clouds of Eastern China Using Multi‐Moment Microphysics Schemes
abstract: The characteristics of supercooled liquid water (SLW) within icing clouds over eastern China are investigated using in situ aircraft observations and numerical simulations. Supercooled liquid water content increases from 0 to −4°C, but decreases sharply below −4°C. Abundant supercooled large droplets (SLD) were observed, with the effective diameter reaching 175 μm ${\upmu }\mathrm{m}$ and number concentration (Nt) exceeding 19 cm−3. An aircraft icing rate and intensity forecast algorithm is proposed by incorporating flight conditions and SLW spectral characteristics, together with a new diagnostic relation between cloud droplet shape parameter and Nt implemented into the three‐moment NSSL scheme. Sensitivity simulations indicate that the improved scheme can reproduce well the temperature‐dependent variation of SLW content, and significantly enhance forecasted rate of icing, intensity, and icing cloud layer depth.

explanation: 该论文研究的是利用SWOT任务提供的海面高度（SSH）观测数据，通过多尺度4DVAR框架进行数据同化，以提高海洋模型对多尺度变率的表征能力。虽然主要关注海洋环境，但SWOT任务本身属于卫星遥感技术，用于获取大气和海洋环境数据，因此与大气环境遥感技术有一定关联。
authors: Chaojie Zhou;Wei Wu;Jungang Yang;Xinhua Zhao;Zhanpeng Zhuang
title: Specialized SWOT SSH Data Assimilation Improves the Representation of Multiscale Variability in the Ocean Model
abstract: The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission provides wide‐swath sea surface height (SSH) observations at scales poorly sampled by conventional altimetry. Assimilating SWOT data remains challenging because part of the short‐wavelength variance may not be dynamically representable by a given model configuration. We therefore develop a two‐step multiscale 4DVAR framework to assimilate real SWOT SSH observations. The first step constrains broad‐scale SSH mismatches, whereas the second assimilates the remaining SWOT information using a shorter decorrelation scale and the first‐step analysis as background. In the northern South China Sea, the multiscale framework reduces SWOT SSH residuals, yields more organized scale‐dependent increments, and improves the representation and forecast persistence of model‐resolved multiscale SSH variability. Independent SST, Argo, and drifter observations further indicate reduced upper‐ocean thermal biases, mainly within the mixed layer. These results demonstrate that scale‐dependent assimilation can make more effective use of SWOT's multiscale information within a finite‐resolution regional model.

explanation: 该论文研究了地磁平静条件下的 Sq 电流系统以及强风暴期间的 Sq 类似中纬度涡旋的持续性和动力学。这涉及到了地球大气层物理和电离层的研究，虽然不直接涉及空气质量监测或卫星观测技术，但与大气环境遥感技术中的电离层成分分析和电流系统研究相关，因此属于高度相关。
authors: Fengjue Wang;Chao Xiong;Yunliang Zhou;Yixun Zhu;Yuyang Huang;Baohua Sun;Bohao Qian;Simin Wang;LinLin Li;Shuji Abe;Akimasa Yoshikawa
title: Persistence and Dynamics of an Sq‐like Mid‐Latitude Current Vortex During the May 2024 Superstorm
abstract: The solar quiet (Sq) current system describes the mid‐latitude equivalent current under quiet geomagnetic conditions, but whether an Sq‐like vortex persists during intense storms remains unclear. Using dense East Asian magnetometer observations, including the Chinese Meridian Project, we reconstruct the storm‐time ionospheric equivalent‐current system during the May 2024 superstorm. Observations reveal a persistent Sq‐like mid‐latitude vortex with enhanced intensity and rapid focus displacement. Its evolution follows the interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) Bz and couples closely with auroral and equatorial currents. Southward IMF Bz enhances magnetospheric convection, driving auroral‐oval expansion and equatorial electrojet intensification that compress the vortex equatorward, whereas northward turnings lead to auroral retreat and counter‐electrojet pulses, which in turn drive the poleward rebound of the mid‐latitude vortex. Our results extend the Tsuji's model by resolving the mid‐latitude vortex, thereby completing the ionospheric current response chain from auroral currents to the Cowling‐enhanced equatorial response.

explanation: 该论文研究了北京地区有机气溶胶（OA）的分子指纹演变，探讨了人为源和生物源排放以及湿度诱导的水相化学对OA的影响。论文使用了提取电喷雾电离飞行时间质谱仪（EESI-TOF-MS）和Aerodyne质谱仪进行空气质量的监测和对大气成分的分析，因此与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
topic_words: ['Organic Aerosol', 'EESI-TOF-MS', 'Aerodyne Mass Spectrometer', 'air quality monitoring', 'atmospheric composition analysis']
authors: Tingting Feng;Tianle Pan;Yingkun Wang;Zi Tao;Shan Huang;Yibo Huangfu;Bin Yuan;Min Shao;Lu Qi;André S. H. Prévôt;Douglas R. Worsnop;Xinming Wang;Weiwei Hu
title: Evolution of Organic Aerosol Molecular Fingerprints in Beijing: Impact of Anthropogenic‐Biogenic Emissions and Humidity‐Induced Aqueous Chemistry
abstract: Organic aerosol (OA) continues to pose a significant challenge in the study of fine particulate matter due to its complex sources and composition. By utilizing the Extractive Electrospray Ionization Time‐of‐Flight Mass Spectrometer (EESI‐TOF‐MS), OA can be identified at a near‐molecular level, which facilitates a deeper understanding of its composition. Intercomparison of OA and specific source tracers between EESI‐TOF‐MS and an Aerodyne Mass Spectrometer (AMS) confirms that EESI‐TOF‐MS can track OA evolution, while the results indicate that the EESI‐TOF‐MS only measures 30%–43% of the OA quantified by the AMS. During the summer campaign conducted in Beijing, CHO was identified as the predominant species, representing 66% of OA. CHON and CHN groups contributed for 27% and 2%, respectively. Molecular fingerprints indicated significant contributions from both anthropogenic (e.g., biomass burning, aromatic oxidation) and biogenic (e.g., monoterpene and sesquiterpene oxidation) sources. By comparing the concentration and composition of OA during polluted and clean periods, it is evident that the pollution was predominantly characterized by organic nitrate (ON) and CHO4‐5 species, linked to enhanced anthropogenic emissions and potentially biogenic sources. Furthermore, machine learning and SHAP analysis identified relative humidity as a critical driver of most OA species. Cluster analysis further resolved these RH‐enhanced ions, which are mainly short‐chain organic acids, into two distinct categories: Cluster 1 driven by early‐morning photochemical and aqueous‐phase processes, and Cluster 2 associated with regional chemistry and sulfate‐mediated reactions. Our findings highlight the synergistic roles of anthropogenic emissions and meteorological conditions in shaping the OA burden and composition, providing crucial molecular‐level insights for refining climate and air quality models.

explanation: 该研究关注北极平流层顶和逆温层的响应，涉及平流层和热带层的相互作用，这对于理解大气成分和空气质量监测具有重要意义。
topic_words: ['tropopause', 'tropopause inversion layer', 'sudden stratospheric warming', 'atmospheric composition', 'air quality monitoring']
authors: Lingyun Yang;Shaodong Zhang;Chunming Huang;Kaiming Huang;Yun Gong;Zheng Ma;Jiahui Luo
title: Category‐Based Composite Analysis of Arctic Tropopause and Tropopause Inversion Layer Responses to Sudden Stratospheric Warmings
abstract: This study investigates the heterogeneous impacts of sudden stratospheric warming (SSW) events on the Arctic tropopause and tropopause inversion layer (TIL) using ERA5 reanalysis data from 1979/1980 to 2022/2023. According to the significance of their TIL and tropopause height responses, all 50 SSW events are classified into five categories: significant major, significant minor, non‐significant major, non‐significant minor, and anomalous minor. 65.4% of major SSWs and 12.5% of minor SSWs have significant impacts on the Arctic tropopause and TIL. Notably, anomalous minor SSWs do not strengthen but weaken the TIL, and do not lower but raise the tropopause height. Building upon the established coupling mechanism between the TIL/tropopause and SSW, we analyze the role of background flow changes: stratospheric planetary wave breaking decelerates background westerlies, causing subsequent planetary waves to break at lower altitudes and amplifying both adiabatic heating that drives tropopause descent and dynamical heating that enhances the TIL. We further provide an explanation for the generation of dynamical heating near the tropopause, which arises from the coexistence of residual mean upwelling anomalies induced by planetary wave divergence anomalies at 7–12 km and residual mean downwelling anomalies induced by planetary wave convergence anomalies above 12 km. The breaking of sufficient upward‐propagating planetary waves in the stratosphere satisfies the key dynamical condition required for significant impacts on the tropopause and TIL. When stratospheric planetary wave convergence anomalies are weaker than the local planetary wave divergence anomalies, the TIL is weakened and the tropopause height rises instead.

explanation: 该论文研究了野火排放的黑碳对北美西部积雪融化的影响，涉及空气质量监测、大气成分分析和气溶胶反演等大气环境遥感技术相关内容，因此与该领域密切相关。
authors: Nilkamal Jaisawal;Cenlin He;Rajesh Kumar;Mark Flanner;Yang Li
title: Impact of Wildfire‐Emitted Black Carbon on Snowmelt Across Western North America
abstract: Wildfires are a major source of black carbon (BC) and their increasing frequency and intensity have enhanced BC deposition onto snowpack across western North America, which accelerates snowmelt and triggers multiple feedbacks that can substantially alter atmospheric composition and regional hydrology. Using the Weather Research and Forecasting model coupled with Chemistry (WRF‐Chem) integrated with the Snow, Ice, and Aerosol Radiative (SNICAR) scheme, we investigate the impacts of fire‐emitted BC on snowmelt following the high‐emission 2021 fire season. Summertime wildfires generate elevated near‐surface BC concentrations, accounting for more than 80% of total near‐surface BC across Alaska, British Columbia, and the Pacific Northwest. During autumn and winter, fire‐emitted BC continues to account for over 50% of atmospheric BC across California, Alaska, and British Columbia. Fire‐emitted BC mass in snow column reaches seasonal domain maximum of 2,828 μg m−2 in winter and 2,978 μg m−2 in spring, accumulating persistently over the western Rockies and coastal mountains. This deposition reduces seasonal mean surface albedo by up to 0.01 in spring across western North America, especially over the Alaska Range, the Rockies, and the Sierra Nevada. The resulting albedo reduction increases solar radiation absorption by the snowpack, reducing seasonal mean snow water equivalent (SWE) by up to 87.3 kg m−2 and enhancing snowmelt by up to 4.28 kg m−2 in spring across the domain, with stronger impacts occurring in spring when increasing solar insolation accelerates snow aging and melt, re‐exposes BC at snow surface, and amplifies absorption through a positive feedback loop.

explanation: 该论文研究微尺度水分聚集和云过渡区对气溶胶性质的影响，涉及卫星观测（如AOD反演）、气溶胶光学厚度和大气成分分析，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Eshkol Eytan;Martin Wirth;Silke Groß;J. Christine Chiu;Graham Feingold
title: Moisture Aggregation and the Cloud Transition Zone Shape Mesoscale Aerosol Properties
abstract: Mesoscale moisture aggregation and cloud organization in shallow convection have gained much attention regarding their role in Earth's energy budget and cloud feedbacks on climate. Because aerosol particles swell in humid air, mesoscale moisture patterns are expected to be accompanied by corresponding variations in aerosol optical depth (AOD). However, observing such patterns is challenging because space‐borne imagers cannot reliably retrieve AOD in the aerosol–cloud transition zone (CTZ), where radiative transfer is different from both clear‐sky and cloudy conditions. By linking the concepts of moisture aggregation and the CTZ, we ask whether mesoscale patterns organize AOD patterns on the mesoscale, and what are the structures and components of the CTZ in different cloud morphologies. We address these questions using space‐borne images complemented by high‐resolution airborne LiDAR acquired during the EUREC4A field campaign, which sampled a range of cloud patterns and aerosol concentrations. We show that small cumulus clouds contribute to the CTZ through local moistening of the cloud layer. As moisture aggregates to support larger clouds, thin detrained layers near the trade‐wind inversion spread at the top of the cloud layer over tens of kilometers and increase AOD while often manifesting as optically thin clouds that would often not be detected by satellites. Such perturbations reverse during dust events, when precipitation‐processed air is cleaner than the background aerosol profile. Our results indicate that expected mesoscale AOD gradients are missing from satellite retrievals and suggest that mesoscale dynamics affect Earth's energy budget through shaping aerosol‐cloud‐radiation interactions.

explanation: 该论文研究了格陵兰岛2024年夏季的极端降水事件，使用了卫星测量数据（GRACE/GRACE-FO）和再分析数据（ERA5），探讨了北太平洋海表温度异常对其的影响。这与大气环境遥感技术中的卫星观测和大气成分分析密切相关，因此是强相关的。
authors: Zhaosheng Zhai;Yetang Wang;Shugui Hou
title: Unprecedented Early‐Summer Precipitation Over the Greenland in 2024, Driven Primarily by the North Pacific Sea Surface Temperature Anomalies
abstract: Extreme precipitation events exert substantial impacts on the Mass Balance (MB) of the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) and its contribution to global sea level, but elucidating their underlying mechanisms remains challenging. This study utilized in situ observations, ERA5 reanalysis, and GRACE/GRACE‐FO satellite measurements to investigate the unprecedented precipitation during early summer 2024 and its drivers. During June–July 2024, stations in southern and eastern Greenland recorded unprecedented precipitation exceeding two standard deviations above the climatological mean, making it the highest early summer precipitation total since the 1940s. Record‐high North Pacific sea surface temperatures (SSTs) during May–June–July 2024 excited Rossby wave trains, which favored anomalous anticyclonic and cyclonic circulations over Greenland. These circulations enhanced oceanic moisture transport and caused frequent atmospheric river landfalls over southern and southeastern Greenland, which, along with orographic uplift, generated precipitation anomalies equivalent to twice the 1991–2020 climatological mean. As a consequence, the strong precipitation (primarily snowfall) and negative temperature anomalies driven by synoptic circulation led to the smallest summer GrIS mass loss since 2002. Our findings highlight the critical role of North Pacific SST anomalies in driving early summer Greenland precipitation extremes, thereby advancing predictive capability for future extreme events and their implications for GrIS MB under persistent North Pacific warming.

explanation: 该论文研究北方 Hemisphere 永久冻土区表层有机碳储量及其未来变化，涉及气候变化对土壤有机碳的影响，虽然不直接提及遥感技术，但使用了机器学习模型估算碳储量，这与大气环境遥感技术中的数据分析方法有一定关联，因此认为其与大气环境遥感技术相关。
authors: Dong Wang;Tonghua Wu;Xiaodong Wu;Shenyun Chen;Hotaek Park;Tetsuya Hiyama;Ren Li;Xiaofan Zhu;Jie Chen;Sizhong Yang;Xianhua Wei;Amin Wen;Yune La;Peiqing Lou;Xuchun Yan;Xin Ma;Xingchen Lin
title: Projection of the Status and Future Shifts of Topsoil Organic Carbon Stocks in Northern Hemisphere Permafrost Regions: Patterns and Drivers
abstract: The Northern Hemisphere (NH) permafrost areas harbor vast reservoirs of soil organic carbon (SOC), which are potentially at serious releasing risk due to climate change. However, projections of future changes in SOC stocks in these regions remain subject to large uncertainties. In this study, we constructed an integrated approach that combines space‐for‐time substitution with a machine learning model to estimate the current status of surface (0–30 cm) SOC stocks in NH permafrost regions and to project their future changes throughout the 21st century under various Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs). The results indicate that approximately 224.2 Pg C were stored in NH permafrost regions during the baseline period (1981–2000), and they will remain relatively stable (−0.5% ± 0.9%) until the conclusion of 21st century under SSP1‐2.6, while a significant loss of about 8.5% ± 3.5% is projected under SSP5‐8.5. Spatially, the areas with increased surface SOC in the future are mainly located in the continuous permafrost zone, while the decrease is identified in most of discontinuous, sporadic, and isolated permafrost areas. Among ecosystems, grasslands and deserts are projected to act as future carbon sinks, while forests exhibit the largest declines. Temperature exerts the strongest control on SOC dynamics in the northern circumpolar (NC) permafrost region through a nonlinear threshold effect, whereas precipitation and vegetation productivity govern SOC changes in the Third Pole. These results highlight pronounced spatial heterogeneity of SOC dynamics in permafrost regions, providing valuable insights for carbon–climate feedback assessments and regional policy.

explanation: 该论文研究了低地球轨道卫星星座的环境影响，特别是温室气体排放，这与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量和大气成分分析密切相关。论文涉及卫星发射、运载火箭生产和再利用对环境的影响，这些都是遥感技术监测和分析的重要领域。
authors: Rushil Kukreja;Edward J. Oughton;Richard Linares
title: Emissions Poised to Rocket: Modeling the Environmental Impacts of Low Earth Orbit Satellite Constellations
abstract: The proliferation of satellite megaconstellations in low Earth orbit represents a significant advancement in global broadband connectivity. However, we urgently need to understand the potential environmental impacts, particularly greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with these constellations. This study addresses a critical gap in modeling current and future GHG emissions by developing an open‐source life cycle assessment methodology, applied to 12 launch vehicles and 24 megaconstellations. Our analysis reveals that fully deploying the 24 constellations would emit about 9.1 Mt CO2. Propellant combustion during launch events (60.9%) and launcher production (31.6%) contribute most significantly to overall GHG emissions, accounting for 92.5% of modeled life cycle emissions. Reusing launch vehicles lowers production emissions per launch by 81%–97% relative to building a new vehicle for every flight, highlighting the environmental benefits of reusability in space technology. The findings underscore the importance of launch vehicle and satellite design choices to minimize potential environmental impacts. The Open‐source Rocket and Constellation Lifecycle Emissions (ORACLE) repository is freely available and aims to facilitate further research in this field. This study provides a critical baseline for policymakers and industry stakeholders to develop strategies for reducing the carbon footprint of the space industry, especially satellite megaconstellations.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术相关，因为它涉及使用遥感技术监测和分析大湖区域冬季气温变化、冰层损失、营养物质通量和温室气体排放等大气环境参数。
topic_words: ['air temperature', 'ice loss', 'nutrient fluxes', 'greenhouse gas emissions', 'lake-effect snowfall']
authors: Marguerite A. Xenopoulos;Claire M. Stevens;Most Shirina Begum;Vedanti Ghatwala;Panditha V. S. L. Gunawardana;James D. Kelley;Carolina N. Koebel;Jessica Livingstone;Sherryann A. Prowell;Yue Zheng;John F. Bratton;Matthew Child;Ian Harding;R. Michael McKay;Ted Ozersky;Samir Qadir;Sapna Sharma;Michael R. Twiss;Mathew G. Wells
title: Vanishing Winters and Shrinking Ice: Ecosystem Services and Societal Impacts in the Laurentian Great Lakes
abstract: The Laurentian Great Lakes are undergoing rapid winter transformations, with profound implications for human societies. Winter air temperatures have increased, accelerating ice loss since the mid‐1990s. These trends are altering thermal regimes, shifting precipitation from snow to rain, and increasing winter runoff and nutrient fluxes, with cascading effects across physical, chemical, and biological systems. Using the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment framework, we synthesize how warming winters affect supporting, regulating, provisioning, and cultural ecosystem services, as well as their positive and negative socioeconomic implications for the Sustainable Development Goals. Winter warming is altering supporting services by reducing the stability and extent of under‐ice habitats that provide refugia for biodiversity and disrupting nutrient cycling. Regulating services are also affected, through increased greenhouse gas emissions, shoreline erosion and flooding, altered disease dynamics and changes in lake‐effect snowfall. Provisioning services, such as freshwater supply and fisheries, are increasingly vulnerable to harmful algal blooms, infrastructure disruptions, and reduced habitat for cold‐water species. Cultural and recreational activities including ice fishing, Indigenous traditions, and winter tourism are also threatened, while unstable ice may increase drowning risks. Although reduced ice cover may benefit navigation and summer recreation, these gains are outweighed by broader ecological and cultural losses. Collectively, these findings show that lake ice functions as a mediating variable regulating interconnected ecological and societal processes. Its loss threatens ecosystem resilience and heightens socioeconomic vulnerabilities for the 40 million people who depend on the Great Lakes. Addressing these challenges will require cross‐border cooperation.

explanation: 该论文研究了斯瓦尔巴群岛附近的海-气相互作用以及气候变化对北大西洋水的影响，涉及海洋和大气系统的相互作用，与大气环境遥感技术中的海洋成分分析和气候变化监测相关。
authors: Yue Wu;David P. Stevens;Xiaoming Zhai;Ian A. Renfrew
title: A Prospective Cooling Machine for the Svalbard Branch of Norwegian Atlantic Water in a Future Climate
abstract: The evolution of air‐sea interaction and the ocean north of Svalbard is investigated using a high‐resolution configuration of the coupled climate model HadGEM3‐GC3.1 under a high‐emission pathway (SSP5‐8.5). To the west and north of Svalbard, where the West Spitsbergen Current—the northward branch of the Norwegian Atlantic Current—carries warm and saline Atlantic Water (AW) into the Arctic, we identify a significant shift in the pattern of sea‐ice decline. In the late 20th century, the sea‐ice edge retreats gradually downstream along the current's pathway. However, in the 21st century, the ice edge retreats northward across the continental slope, leading to the simultaneous exposure of the AW core to the atmosphere. This rapid increased exposure triggers enhanced cooling and convective mixing along the AW pathway. The water column undergoes destratification due to the AW encroachment, along with mixing, resulting in a warmer and less stratified upper ocean downstream on this pathway. The potential temperature maximum of the AW shoals, increasing the potential for enhanced oceanic heat loss. A closed regional ocean heat content analysis reveals that net advective heat convergence into the region increases substantially, driving a sustained wintertime surface heat loss that stabilizes at ∼70 TW by the 2040 s. These changes suggest that a prospective “cooling machine” north of Svalbard will soon emerge in a future climate, operating at a capacity comparable to the Barents Sea and fundamentally altering the water mass transformation and heat export into the deep Arctic interior.

explanation: 该论文主要关注的是预测电力线引起的火灾发生的可能性及其早期蔓延，涉及火灾气象、燃料和地形等环境因素，但并未涉及大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测或大气成分分析等。
authors: Xuezheng Zong;Xianli Wang;Mike D. Flannigan
title: Prediction of Escaped Powerline‐Caused Fires in Alberta, Canada
abstract: Powerlines have increasingly become a source of wildfire ignitions, contributing to more escaped and catastrophic fires during extreme fire weather. Temporary power shutoffs are implemented to reduce this risk, yet decisions on their implementations are often based on limited scientific evidence. Focusing on the boreal forests in Alberta, Canada, we developed an integrated framework to assess the likelihood of Escaped powerline‐caused fires (EPF) (EPFs) from occurrence and early spread perspectives. Using records of powerline‐caused fires from 1990 to 2023, we integrated MaxEnt and machine‐learning models to predict occurrence and escape probability from fire weather, fuels, and topography at the regional scale, overcoming the reliance on detailed powerline operational parameters. Although the frequency of powerline‐caused fires has increased in recent decades, most fires remain small and are contained during initial attack (IA). Fire weather emerged as the primary drivers of both fire occurrence probability and spread. Higher fire weather substantially increases the probability of powerline‐caused fire occurrence, while fires in coniferous forests are more likely to escape initial attacks. Under extreme fire weather (Fire Weather Index (FWI) >30), the EPF likelihood is more than three times higher than under moderate conditions (5 ≤ FWI <11), with the significant increases concentrated in southwestern Alberta.

explanation: 该论文主要研究如何利用消费级智能手表通过人工智能技术检测高血压，虽然涉及信号处理和生物医学监测，但与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演等）无关。
authors: Paolo Di Achille;Lawrence Cai;Jiang Wu;Mingwu Gao;Bhavna Daryani;Jonathan Wang;Utkarsh Khanna;Ho Ko;Anupam Pathak;Mark Malhotra;Shwetak Patel;Jacqueline B. Shreibati;Stephen P. Juraschek;Pramod Rudrapatna;Matthew Thompson;Ming-Zher Poh
title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch
abstract:
Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch 
 Hypertension is a silent killer, with over half of affected adults unaware of their condition1,2. This lack of awareness is a major concern, as early intervention is critical for preventing major adverse cardiovascular events3,4. Here we show that applying artificial intelligence (AI) to multimodal waveforms (photoplethysmography and accelerometry) recorded using a widely available consumer smartwatch (AI-PPG-ACC-HTN), without any cuff calibration, can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure (BP) devices in the existing clinical framework. We validated AI-PPG-ACC-HTN in a prospective, multicenter study of 196 diverse participants free from known cardiovascular disease and antihypertensive medication against gold-standard 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days of real-world monitoring, AI-PPG-ACC-HTN detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8% (95% CI, 54.0%-76.3%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 80.6% (95% CI, 68.6%-89.6%). In comparison, initial office BP screening achieved a sensitivity of 55.3% (95% CI, 43.4%-66.7%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%) and PPV of 77.8% (95% CI, 64.4%-88.0%). These results highlight an opportunity for consumer smartwatches to facilitate population-level opportunistic hypertension screening by prompting at-risk individuals toward clinical assessment and confirmatory diagnosis using established cuff-based methodologies, offering an accessible tool to address this major public health challenge.

explanation: 该论文主要关注中国如何通过氢及其衍生物实现成本有效的碳中和，涉及能源经济转型和可再生能源部署，但并未明确提及大气环境遥感技术、空气质量监测、卫星观测或大气成分分析等具体技术内容，因此与大气环境遥感技术相关性较弱。
authors: Xinyu Chen;Xinyang Guo;Xi Yang;Jiashuo Li;Michael McElroy
title: Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China
abstract:
Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China 
 The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recommended 1.5°C carbon reduction target, requiring powerful enforcement from major economies. China, the largest CO2 emitter, is facing severe difficulties for both variable renewable accommodation and decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. Here, we present cost-effective carbon-neutral transition pathways for entire energy economy of China emphasizing the significant role of hydrogen and derivatives as green energy carriers, considering high-resolution renewable deployments, hourly power system operations in 29 provincial regions, over 46,000 rail/road/marine/pipeline transfer routing of hydrogen derivatives, process-level fuel adoption strategies in all end-use sectors. Results show that incorporating hydrogen and derivatives can reduce the overall transition cost by $ 10.7 trillion compared with renewable and electrification pathways, achieving negative carbon abatement costs ($-6.15/ton), eliminating external oil import expenses, equivalent to over 50% of China trade surplus (2023 level)1, significantly boosting employment and economic growth. title: Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer
abstract:
Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer 
 Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) is a fundamental photoinduced process that underpins a broad range of energy- or electron-transfer events1,2. In the absence of productive substrate engagement, the MLCT excited state typically relaxes to the ground state via photophysical deactivation, reflecting its largely reversible character3,4. Here we report a class of isolable copper–heteroaryl sulfone complexes that, upon visible light irradiation, undergo an irreversible MLCT-driven fragmentation through C–S bond cleavage within the coordinated sulfone ligand, generating carbon-centered radicals. Spectroscopic and computational studies support the formation of MLCT-derived excited states and a low-barrier pathway for C–S bond cleavage. This reactivity is largely independent of the reduction potentials of the corresponding free sulfones, enabling the generation of fluoroalkyl and non-fluorinated tertiary, secondary, and primary (even methyl) alkyl radicals. We demonstrate the utility of this platform in copper-catalyzed C–H fluoroalkylation of arenes and terminal alkynes. Leveraging these MLCT-generated trifluoromethyl radicals to initiate halogen-atom transfer (XAT) from perfluorocyclobutyl iodide (I-FCB), we also achieve radical perfluorocyclobutylation–iodination of alkenes, addressing a longstanding challenge in the incorporation of perfluorocyclobutyl motifs.

title: A two-dimensional reticular triaxial molecularly woven fabric
abstract:
A two-dimensional reticular triaxial woven network material is constructed by incorporating C3-symmetric macrocycles into a triangular weave pattern, enabling an extra topological dimension to be used for the construction of functional materials. 
 Inspired by macroscopic weaving techniques1–4, molecular weaving, which interlaces molecular strands into ordered networks, has emerged as a powerful strategy for designing functional materials with emergent properties5,6. However, so far, molecular weaving has relied mainly on linear building blocks and biaxial structures. Higher-order weaving (≥3 axes) of nonlinear building blocks is expected to produce intriguing architectures and bring new and unforeseen functions to the resulting materials; however, their construction and property investigation remain underexplored. Here we report a two-dimensional reticular triaxial woven polymer network constructed by incorporating C3-symmetric macrocycles into the woven structure through dative B–N polymerization. The resulting material not only exhibits unique topological chirality and robust mechanical properties but it also serves as a porous material that permits the separation of representative aromatic/aliphatic compounds. This functional utility highlights how higher-order triaxial woven topologies can provide unique advantages in terms of regulating material properties and introduces an extra topological dimension for the construction of functional materials. A two-dimensional reticular triaxial woven network material is constructed by incorporating C3-symmetric macrocycles into a triangular weave pattern, enabling an extra topological dimension to be used for the construction of functional materials.

title: Accelerating commercialization and deployment of indoor photovoltaics
abstract:
Recent progress in photovoltaics has been investigated to translate state-of-the-art cells in the laboratory into deployable products suited to real indoor conditions, focusing on wide-bandgap absorbers, reduced non-radiative voltage losses and reshaping module design. 
 The growing reliance on distributed electronics, such as Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, smart-home devices and portable consumer products, has intensified demand for indoor energy-harvesting technologies that reduce battery replacement and servicing. Consequently, indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have advanced rapidly; however, translating state-of-the-art cells into deployable products requires design principles that reflect real indoor conditions. Here recent progress in perovskite (bulk and quantum dot), organic, amorphous-silicon, III–V and dye-sensitized PVs is examined to identify bottlenecks that arise under low-light conditions and during scale-up. This Review highlights how low-light operation favours wide-bandgap absorbers and reduced non-radiative voltage losses while reshaping module design: lower series-resistance (RS) penalties permit wider subcells and fewer interconnections, increasing geometric fill factor, whereas shunt and leakage pathways consume more of the weak photocurrent. Measurement practices for credible cross-technology benchmarking are discussed, emphasizing the transparent reporting of spectra, illuminance/irradiance, stabilization and uncertainty. Finally, the relationship between device performance and manufacturability and product integration is considered, including power-management requirements and chemical/regulatory constraints (for example, restricted substances and end-of-life handling). These guidelines provide a practical framework for evaluating indoor PVs on the basis of delivered and retained power and for accelerating the transition from laboratory-scale demonstrations to reliable, visually adaptable products for the built environment. Recent progress in photovoltaics has been investigated to translate state-of-the-art cells in the laboratory into deployable products suited to real indoor conditions, focusing on wide-bandgap absorbers, reduced non-radiative voltage losses and reshaping module design.

title: In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs
abstract:
Using high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double knockout screening, synergistic gene combinations to improve CAR-T cell therapy are revealed. 
 Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, but its efficacy remains limited by multiple negative regulatory mechanisms intrinsic to T cells1–4. Here we perform a high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout (DKO) CRISPR screen, and identify multiple DKO gene pairs that are both effective and synergistic. The top pair, NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO, has multiple favourable immunological features. Whole-transcriptome profiling and in vivo single-cell RNA sequencing reveal that NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO specifically upregulates metabolic pathways in CAR-T cells, which show significantly higher metabolic fitness and mitochondrial activity. NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO CAR-T cells and T cells exhibit exceptionally potent antitumour efficacy and long-term tumour control across different tumour models without compromising safety features. NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO outperforms several benchmark single-gene and dual-gene modifications in T cells and CAR-T cells5–9. These data demonstrate high-throughput in vivo CAR-T DKO screening for rapid discovery of combination targets, and establish NR4A1–SOCS3 as a promising pair of intracellular checkpoints to engineer high-performance CAR-T therapies against cancer. Using high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double knockout screening, synergistic gene combinations to improve CAR-T cell therapy are revealed.

title: Observation of prethermal dynamical phase transitions and resonant melting
abstract:
A programmable neutral-atom quantum simulator is used to explore quench dynamics in spin models with up to 180 qubits, revealing prethermal dynamical phase transitions and resonant melting. 
 The dynamics of isolated quantum systems following a sudden quench has a central role in many areas of material science, high-energy physics and quantum chemistry1–4. Such far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics—which features complex phenomena with implications for thermalization, non-equilibrium phase transitions and Floquet phase engineering5–8—is challenging to study numerically, in particular, in high-dimensional systems9,10. Here we use a programmable neutral-atom quantum simulator11 to systematically explore quench dynamics in spin models with up to 180 qubits. By initializing the system in a product state and performing quenches across a broad parameter space, we discover several stable, qualitatively distinct dynamical regimes. We trace their robustness to Floquet-like prethermal steady states8 that are stabilized over exponentially long emergent timescales by strong dynamical constraints. We further observe sharp peaks in the dynamical response that are quantitatively explained by the structured melting of prethermalization through resonances. In two dimensions, we uncover a prethermally driven, first-order dynamical phase transition linked to the proliferation of Néel-order defects6,12, and probe it quantitatively using a generalized Clausius–Clapeyron test. Together, these results establish a programmable route to high-energy prethermal phase structure: long-lived dynamical phases, their resonant breakdown and a first-order dynamical phase transition that is not inherited from the equilibrium phase boundaries. A programmable neutral-atom quantum simulator is used to explore quench dynamics in spin models with up to 180 qubits, revealing prethermal dynamical phase transitions and resonant melting.
