title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply
abstract: Dansgaard-Oeschger (DO) events during the last ice age are thought to reflect rapid shifts in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Greenland ice cores suggest warming transitions within only a few decades—or even just over 10 years. Using precisely dated speleothem oxygen-isotope records from the Asian monsoon region, we have shown that the same DO warmings unfolded over more than a century. Isotope modeling revealed that Greenland records primarily capture a rapid atmospheric reorganization triggered by the initial sea-ice retreat in the northeastern North Atlantic, whereas the parallel AMOC recovery and hemispheric thermal adjustment proceeded much more slowly. These findings reveal that natural AMOC transitions evolved more slowly than the rapid North Greenland oxygen-isotope shifts would imply, thereby refining our understanding of “abruptness” during DO events.

title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients’ plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance ofBacteroides xylanisolvens, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.

title: Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago
abstract: Cannabis is the world’s most-used illicit psychoactive plant, yet direct prehistoric evidence for its consumption is rare. In this study, we present the earliest direct evidence of cannabis use: offerings of plant parts and chemical compounds in ancient human hair recovered from a monumental tomb in Siberia. The findings suggest that the plant was used for its psychoactive qualities across Eurasia, where specific wild populations might have had naturally higher active compound levels. We show that the practice of cannabis consumption dates back at least 2800 years, anchoring debates around contemporary usage and informing discussions on cannabis in medicine, public health, law, and industry.

title: Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake
abstract: How and when the subduction megathrust recovers its locking state after a great earthquake is important to understanding earthquake-cycle physics and future hazards. Here we report the delineation of the relocking process after the 2011 magnitude 9 Tohoku earthquake with 14 years of postseismic seafloor geodetic observations. These data, combined with onshore geodetic observations, analyses of repeating earthquakes, and numerical modeling, reveal how the recovery of locking is interrupted by afterslip on the megathrust and accompanied by stress relaxation in the viscoelastic upper mantle. The results indicate that the megathrust has already arrived at a locking state today similar to that before the earthquake despite the ongoing stress relaxation. The acquired knowledge aids understanding of megathrust earthquake cycles at other subduction zones.

title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children’s everyday speech
abstract: Children learn to understand and speak from the speech around them, yet how that everyday input shapes learning remains unresolved. Large language models show that language is learnable from data, but their scale and training conditions differ sharply from a child’s natural experience. We trained cognitively feasible, child-specific models on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1000 days of life. Each model learned incrementally from a single child’s ordered speech input without prior linguistic knowledge, developing phoneme-like and word-form representations that tracked each child’s learning pace. Learning was dependent on dense daily sampling and replay of recent input, indicating that both experience- and memory-related processes are necessary. These findings show that everyday experience contains sufficient structure for language learning and establish child-specific modeling for testing developmental theories.

title: Denoising the US Census: Succinct block hierarchical regression
abstract: The 2020 United States Census adopted differential privacy to protect individual confidentiality, adding calibrated noise to summary demographic measurements that are then reconciled into population tables. We developed BlueDown, a postprocessing algorithm that combines techniques from linear regression and constrained optimization while exploiting measurement structure for efficiency. On 2020 Census data, BlueDown reduced the error of groupings by race at the county level by 21 to 36% and of all county-level groupings by 9 to 58%; at the tract level, it reduced error of groupings by housing type by 38 to 61%. These gains came at no cost to confidentiality or computational efficiency and would improve the validity of research relying on this definitive dataset and analyses used to guide the distribution of more than $1.5 trillion in annual federal spending.

title: Quantum gas microscopy of three-flavor Hubbard systems
abstract: Hubbard systems are paradigmatic realizations of strongly correlated many-body systems. Introducing additional species breaks the SU(2) symmetry of the Hubbard model and leads to a wide variety of new exotic quantum phases. Here, we extended quantum gas microscopy to three-flavor Fermi lattice gases in the Hubbard regime. Relying on site- and flavor-resolved detection, we studied the phase diagram of the three-flavor Hubbard model and found signatures of flavor-selective localization and selective pairing at temperatures down to the tunneling energy scale. Our measurements were then compared with numerical linked-cluster expansion calculations. Further increase of phase space density may enable the observation of a distinct pair Mott phase at half filling and shows a path toward the study of color superfluidity and other aspects of quantum chromodynamics.

title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat
abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a rapidly expanding global pollutant, but its effects across biological levels from individuals to ecosystems remain unquantified. We conducted phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species with ranges that span six continents. Noise altered at least one physiological, developmental, or behavioral trait in 80% of species studied, with declines in fitness and abundance and disruptions of predator-prey interactions. Effects occurred in every habitat, although response mechanisms varied for some traits and species, creating winners and losers. Only multispecies analyses can reveal such species- and ecosystem-level impacts of anthropogenic stressors. Our results establish noise as a novel selection pressure reshaping ecosystem dynamics and as a pervasive stressor requiring soundscape protection alongside habitat conservation.

title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling
abstract: Elastocaloric cooling (eC) uses shape memory alloys (SMAs) as energy-efficient, eco-friendly refrigerants. However, cost-effectively fabricating SMAs into fatigue-resistant, heat transfer–enhanced structures remains a key obstacle to commercialization of the eC technology. We introduce a “stamping and stacking” (S-S) method for producing porous, fatigue-resistant SMA structures. Honeycomb-like chips are stamped from nitinol (NiTi) thin sheets and then stacked into a layered tubular structure to increase heat exchange surface and at the same time avoid buckling and splitting failures encountered in existing SMA structures. The stacked structure endures >108compression cycles and can deliver high specific cooling power of 3850 watts per kilogram. Our S-S method reduces fabrication costs by one order of magnitude compared with existing approaches, enabling mass production of eC refrigerant structures for commercial deployment.

title: When fat adapts: From physiological remodeling to disease
abstract: Adipose tissue undergoes extensive remodeling to adapt to changing physiological demands. This plasticity encompasses changes in adipocyte metabolism and number, extracellular matrix organization, vascularization, immune composition, and innervation. When coordinated, these processes preserve energy buffering, thermogenesis, endocrine function, and local tissue support. Pathological adipose tissue remodeling drives obesity-related complications and contributes to many diseases involving organ-associated adipose depots throughout the body. In cancer, tumor-associated fat can develop a metabolic and fibroinflammatory niche that promotes tumor growth and invasion, and remodeling of other depots can directly disrupt neighboring tissues. Recent studies have identified mesenchymal, immune, vascular, and adipocyte states that govern adaptive or pathological outcomes. These findings broaden therapeutic goals beyond reducing fat mass toward restoring adipogenesis, substrate turnover, thermogenic capacity, and tissue-niche function.

title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)–based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

title: Obesity management medications: The way forward
abstract: Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic progressive condition. The altered biological mechanisms that cause obesity frequently require long-term treatment, including pharmacotherapies or bariatric surgery. In recent decades, the pathophysiology of obesity has been understood to an extent that obesity management medication (OMM) discovery could be rationally pursued. Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

title: Cooper’s Ferry/Nipéhe, stratigraphic integrity, and confirming early inland dispersal: Evaluating peopling of the Americas modeling
abstract: Statistical models shape debates over the timing and geography of the initial peopling of the Americas, but their value depends on testing their assumptions against archaeological evidence. We examine the Apparent Stratigraphic Integrity Index (ASI), used to infer postdepositional mixing at Late Pleistocene sites and support a relatively late occupation of temperate North America. ASI describes vertical discontinuity in binned artifact-frequency profiles; it does not directly measure artifact movement or stratigraphic integrity. At Cooper’s Ferry/Nipéhe, Idaho, the 5-centimeter absolute-elevation bins used to calculate ASI do not reflect the actual stratigraphic positions of artifacts across the irregular LU2 surface on which LU3 loess accumulated. The resulting ASI value cannot support claims of large-scale vertical mixing. Independent chronological, stratigraphic, pedogenic, archaeological, and excavation evidence supports the integrity of the ∼16,000–calibrated-years-before-the-present occupation. Cooper’s Ferry/Nipéhe provides early inland evidence expected under coastal-migration models, showing that models should be evaluated against archaeological evidence rather than used to override it.

title: Enigmatic HCl detections as a potential signature of igneous activity on Mars
abstract: Mars is reputed to lack ongoing volcanic activity. However, marsquakes were revealed recently, and clues to volcanism younger than tens of million years have accumulated. While sulfur dioxide, so far undetected, could testify to ongoing eruptive activity, evidence of active magma chambers may be better identified by seepage of halogen gases, such as hydrogen chloride (HCl). Observations by Atmospheric Chemistry Suite led to the widespread observations of HCl at part-per-billion levels in the atmosphere of Mars during the warm perihelion period, attributed to aerosol-atmospheric sources. Here, we report HCl detections during the cold aphelion season that are isolated in the Alba Mons region. We also identify fresh and narrow (<1 meter) fissures in this area, which we interpret to be potential HCl pathways rooted into magmatic bodies at depth. Our results are best explained by ongoing igneous processes in the Martian interior.

title: METTL3-mediated m6A modification of DNMT1 enhances ovarian cancer progression
abstract: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), the most lethal subtype of ovarian cancer, is often diagnosed at advanced stages and remains associated with poor clinical outcome. In this study, we identify a critical oncogenic role of the RNA methyltransferase METTL3 and theN6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification pathway in HGSOC. Suppression of METTL3, either genetically or pharmacologically, and depletion of its binding partner METTL14 impair ovarian cancer proliferation and tumor progression. Mechanistically, we show that METTL3-mediated m6A deposition enhances the translation of DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1), the primary maintenance DNA methyltransferase responsible for preserving genome-wide methylation patterns and silencing tumor suppressor genes. Pharmacological inhibition of DNMT1 induces widespread DNA hypomethylation and up-regulation of the tumor suppressors TNFAIP3 and FBXO32. Consistently, METTL3 suppression reduces DNMT1 abundance and derepresses TNFAIP3 and FBXO32 expression. Knockdown and rescue studies further reveal that DNMT1 primarily mediates METTL3-dependent regulation of cell migration, whereas the antiproliferative effects of METTL3 suppression are likely driven by additional downstream targets. Collectively, these findings identify the m6A-METTL3-DNMT1 axis as a mechanistic link between RNA and DNA methylation pathways and a potential therapeutic vulnerability in HGSOC.

title: Stony coral symbioses show variable responses to future ocean conditions
abstract: Coral reefs support over a quarter of marine species and nearly a billion people worldwide but are also among the ecosystems most threatened by anthropogenic impacts. There is long-standing debate about whether coral symbioses will be disrupted or respond adaptively under future ocean conditions. Using a factorial 2.5-year future-ocean mesocosm experiment across eight coral species representing the major coral lineages, we tracked symbiont community shifts within replicate fragments from the same individual coral. Some corals exhibited stochastic divergence, whereas others showed deterministic shifts in symbiont community composition. Heat stress generally reduced symbiont diversity and promoted predictable restructuring, consistent with deterministic adaptation to moderate thermal stress but stochastic accumulation of diversity under extreme conditions. We propose that adaptive and stochastic responses represent endpoints along a continuum of host-orchestrated symbiont sorting. This study bridges coral reef ecology with broader host-microbiome theory, offering an integrated perspective on how symbiotic systems may respond to environmental change.

title: A functional connectome identifies vulnerability to cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease progression
abstract: Identifying the neurobiological basis of cognitive vulnerability is essential for preventing Alzheimer’s disease (AD). We derived the Alzheimer’s Resilience-Vulnerability Connectome (ARC) by contrasting SuperAgers (SA), an extreme phenotype of preserved late-life memory, with AD using resting-state fMRI. ARC distinguished SA from AD in a discovery cohort (N= 290; AUC = 0.85) and replicated independently (N= 143), involving prefrontal, temporal, and insular networks and associating with brain age. Applied to cognitively unimpaired adults (discovery:N= 818; replication:N= 497), ARC-based subtyping revealed SA-like and AD-like subgroups with comparable baseline cognition but divergent longitudinal trajectories. AD-like individuals exhibited faster cognitive decline, greater amyloid-β accumulation, and higher AD conversion risk. Exploratory GWAS nominatedCLYBLandFRMD6as candidate novel loci associated with the subtype difference. These findings suggest that ARC captures a continuous connectomic dimension of cognitive aging spanning SA, cognitively typical aging, and AD, highlighting the potential of functional connectomic variation for early risk stratification in AD.

title: Local translational program at the muscle-tendon junction endows domain identity in muscle syncytia
abstract: How cells establish specialized subdomains is a fundamental question in cell and tissue biology. Skeletal muscle fibers, among the largest cells in the body, are multinucleated and form distinct regions such as the neuromuscular and myotendinous junctions (MTJs), the latter forming a critical interface between muscle and tendon that transmits contractile force. While transcriptional heterogeneity among myonuclei has been described, whether local translation contributes to domain identity remains unknown, largely due to the lack of tools for domain-specific manipulation. Here, we introduce MTJ-AAV, a viral system that enables selective genetic targeting of MTJ myonuclei. This approach allowed MTJ-specific ribosome tagging and revealed extensive translational regulation underlying MTJ biology and its remodeling during exercise. Untranslated regions of these transcripts were sufficient to control regionalized translation. Notably, the Krüpper-like factor–family transcription factors emerged as translationally up-regulated targets at the MTJ, where they drive local gene expression. Our findings establish local translation as a key layer of subcellular specialization and provide a versatile toolkit for dissecting spatial molecular regulation within muscle syncytia.

title: Clinically derived micro- and nanoplastic uptake drives spatiotemporally confined metabolic stress revealed by bond-selective imaging
abstract: Although microplastics and nanoplastics (MPs/NPs) are pervasive environmental contaminants, our understanding of cellular toxicity remains incomplete, as adverse effects are often attributed to long-term intracellular accumulation, while the spatiotemporal onset of cellular damage remains poorly defined. Here, we use chemical bond–selective stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy and cell models that decouple continuous exposure from intracellular retention to directly visualize clinically derived MP/NP-cell interactions. Cellular stress occurs primarily during MP/NP exposure, accompanied by alterations in lipid droplet (LD) composition. In contrast, following extracellular removal, intracellularly retained MP/NP become largely inert, with recovery of lipid metabolism and cellular functions. Lipidomics identifies arachidonic acid (AA) as a key dysregulated metabolite, and SRS imaging further reveals transient, spatially confined AA enrichment in MP/NP–proximal LDs during uptake. Phospholipid coating of MP/NP attenuates LD alterations and cytotoxicity while preserving particle internalization, establishing uptake-driven metabolic stress, rather than long-term intracellular retention, as a primary source of MP/NP–induced damage.

title: Persistent bistability of Nordic Seas overflow waters over 800,000 years
abstract: The stability of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major uncertainty in projections of future climate. However, direct evidence for AMOC tipping behavior on orbital timescales remains scarce. Here, we reconstruct the strength of Iceland-Scotland Overflow Water, a key lower branch of the deep Atlantic circulation, over the past 800,000 years by combining 12 current-speed records from North Atlantic sediment cores with a data-driven hybrid model. The resulting reconstruction reveals persistent alternation between weak (glacial) and strong (interglacial) circulation modes, pervasive millennial-scale variability within both regimes, and systematic asymmetry between weak-to-strong recoveries and strong-to-weak collapses. Threshold and phase-space analyses show that regime shifts occur within a narrow window of atmospheric carbon dioxide and sea level and often follow hysteresis-like loops. Although bistability persists throughout the last 800,000 years, its sensitivity and timing evolve through time. These findings provide long-term, high-resolution, data-driven constraints on the bistability of Nordic Seas overflow waters and its implications for AMOC resilience in a warming world.

title: On-going retinal neuronal degeneration despite clinical stability in glaucoma
abstract: Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, involves progressive retinal ganglion cell loss. Early detection of this neurodegeneration is critical, yet current clinical methods often identify disease only after substantial damage has occurred. This preliminary study used high-resolution adaptive optics–optical coherence tomography (AO-OCT) to track individual retinal ganglion cells in patients and healthy volunteers over 3 to 5 years. Results revealed higher neurodegeneration in glaucoma compared to normal aging. We observed 4.16 to 6.86% annual decrease in cell density in glaucoma, far exceeding the 0.27% cell loss rate observed in the healthy volunteer group. Critically, AO-OCT detected progression significantly earlier, identifying cell loss 0.74 years before conventional OCT and 1.49 years before visual field testing. These findings demonstrate AO-OCT as a more sensitive tool capable of monitoring glaucomatous damage with superior precision, potentially representing a major advancement over current clinical imaging.

title: Oxygen-mediated projection microstereolithography for sub–100-μm zirconia dental veneers
abstract: High-resolution vat photopolymerization of ceramics is constrained by light scattering, which broadens cured features, and by shallow penetration, which limits interlayer bonding. This trade-off is particularly damaging for microscale structures such as no-preparation dental veneers. We introduce an oxygen-mediated projection microstereolithography strategy in which an oxygen-permeable release film creates an interfacial inhibition field in high-solid–loading zirconia slurry. Rather than uniformly reducing curing, oxygen preferentially filters low-dose scattered light at pattern edges while preserving curing in the projected core. This anisotropic inhibition reshapes the accuracy-depth trade-off, enabling optimized multilayer printing of thin-wall zirconia. The process enabled reproducible fabrication of ∼80-micrometer zirconia veneers with high trueness, improved marginal adaptation, and handling-related strength comparable to substantially thicker milled veneers. The approach provides the potential for minimally invasive dental restoration and a general strategy for high-resolution additive manufacturing of strongly scattering ceramic suspensions.

title: BCLAF1 links RNA splicing to ATF4-dependent metabolic adaptation in acute myeloid leukemia
abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is driven by genetic alterations and non-mutational mechanisms that disrupt normal hematopoiesis and support leukemic cell survival. While the mutational landscape of AML is well characterized, the non-genetic processes sustaining leukemic maintenance remain less understood. Using human AML cells and murine models, we identify BCL2-associated transcription factor 1 (BCLAF1) as a key regulator of leukemic progression through control of mRNA processing. BCLAF1 physically associates with core spliceosome components and regulates alternative splicing programs in leukemic cells. Mechanistically, BCLAF1 is required for productive splicing of activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) mRNA, thereby sustaining ATF4 protein levels and downstream metabolic gene expression programs. Loss of BCLAF1 reduces ATF4 levels, leading to impaired de novo amino acid biosynthesis and increased sensitivity to venetoclax. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized mechanism linking RNA splicing control to metabolic adaptation in AML, identifying BCLAF1 as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

title: Engineered synbiotic microspheres enable system-level reprogramming of the gut-immune-vascular axis in chronic inflammatory vascular disease
abstract: Chronic inflammatory vascular diseases are increasingly recognized as systemic disorders sustained by maladaptive cross-organ immunometabolic coupling, yet current therapeutic strategies remain largely lesion-centered and fail to address upstream drivers of disease persistence. Here, we identify the gut-immune-vascular axis as a system-level pathogenic unit that integrates gut microbial dysbiosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, metabolic imbalance, and vascular immune activation into a self-reinforcing pathological circuit. Through integrated clinical profiling and cross-species validation, we demonstrate that disruption of this axis is characterized by coordinated probiotic depletion, expansion of proinflammatory taxa, translocation of microbial endotoxins, accumulation of microbiota-derived metabolites, and macrophage polarization toward a proinflammatory phenotype along the gut-vascular continuum. To therapeutically target this axis, we engineer enzyme-responsive synbiotic microspheres that codeliver probiotics, a microbial metabolic pathway inhibitor, and a prebiotic within a protective polymeric matrix, enabling site-specific intestinal activation and coordinated microbiota-metabolic modulation. This engineered system restores intestinal barrier integrity, reprograms microbial ecology and metabolite output, suppresses immunometabolic dysfunction, and robustly attenuates pathological vascular remodeling across cellular, murine, and large-animal models, with in-stent restenosis serving as a representative disease context. Collectively, this work establishes axis-oriented immunometabolic reprogramming as a generalizable therapeutic paradigm and highlights engineered synbiotic platforms as scalable tools for system-level intervention in chronic inflammatory diseases.

title: Hoxa10 governs lifelong skeletal stem cell maintenance and bone repair
abstract: Skeletal stem and progenitor cells (SSPCs) sustain bone homeostasis and regeneration throughout life, yet the transcriptional programs that preserve their identity remain poorly defined. Here we identify the distal Hox geneHoxa10as a cell-autonomous regulator of skeletal stem cell maintenance. Using inducible genetic deletion, lineage tracing, single-cell transcriptomics, and injury models, we show that loss ofHoxa10leads to progressive depletion of SSPCs, impaired bone regeneration, and defective matrix organization. Mechanistically,Hoxa10maintains the undifferentiated state of skeletal stem cells by restraining premature osteogenic, adipogenic, and chondrogenic commitment, while promoting collagen III production and collagen fiber alignment within regenerative niches.Hoxa10-dependent regulation of extracellular matrix composition is restricted to primitive progenitors and is uncoupled from osteoblast differentiation. Notably, transient depletion of distal Hox genes in primary human SSPCs recapitulates the murine defects in proliferation, self-renewal, and differentiation restraint. Together, these findings define a conserved Hox-dependent program that preserves skeletal stem cell identity and regenerative competence, revealing how developmental transcription factors are repurposed to sustain the adult skeleton across the life span.

title: Ultrasound neural interface enabling acute spinal cord monitoring and blood flow modulation
abstract: The days following decompression surgery for acute spinal cord injury (SCI) are a critical period for postoperative monitoring. After wound closure, clinicians lack on-demand access to local spinal cord morphology and hemodynamics, and care therefore remains guided largely by systemic surrogates rather than direct postoperative insight into the injured cord. We present the Multimodal Ultrasound System for Injury Care (MUSIC), a temporary epidural ultrasound neural interface placed during standard decompression surgery to enable postoperative brightness-mode imaging, Doppler-derived hemodynamic monitoring, and future device-integrated ultrasound actuation. Across simulations, benchtop, human cadaveric, and porcine studies, MUSIC enabled on-demand visualization of cord structure, hematoma tracking, detection and longitudinal tracking of localized Doppler flow signatures attributable to the sulcal artery region, and, in healthy pigs, proof-of-concept focused ultrasound modulation of blood-flow velocity. MUSIC establishes a temporary postoperative acoustic interface that provides spinal cord information to inform monitoring, future management, and localized intervention strategies after SCI.

title: Common transcriptional changes in the brain during hibernation and Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Hibernation demands rapid brain adaptations, involving cycles of reduced metabolic rate during torpor, followed by brief periods of arousal. Previous studies show hibernation induces a drastic increase in Tau hyperphosphorylation, but a mechanistic connection to disease remains unclear. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing on hippocampi of golden hamsters, we unveil large transcriptional shifts across the hibernation cycle in all cell types, especially glia. Common transcriptional changes in mitochondrial and ribosomal genes are observed in all different cell types. In addition, hibernation triggers an inflammatory-like response in microglia that in part resembles cell states observed in Alzheimer’s disease, but here in the absence of Aβ-accumulation and neurodegeneration. These findings reveal brain transformations that might help preserve vital functions under extreme conditions and they suggest that early cellular changes in AD may be a natural adaptive process.

title: Genetic dissection of cell type–specific congenital heart disease variants reveals ETS1 control of vascular smooth muscle cell fate
abstract: Numerous congenital heart disease (CHD) risk variants lie in cis-regulatory elements, yet the impact of variants in repressed and bivalent chromatin on cell type–specific heart development is unclear. Here, we generated a single-cell multiomic atlas of human cardiac differentiation by jointly profiling H3K27ac, H3K27me3, H3K4me3, and transcriptomes in individual cells, classifying cis-regulatory elements into six chromatin states, enabling prioritization of 610 CHD-associated noncoding variants enriched in lineage- and state-specific regulatory elements, including repressive and bivalent regions. CRISPR knockin of selected variants perturbed nearby gene expression and impaired cardiac differentiation. Dissection of a Polycomb-marked variant nearETS1(ETS proto-oncogene 1) revealed local H3K27me3 loss, H3K27ac gain, and ETS1 up-regulation, which redirects differentiation toward second-heart-field progenitors with epithelial characteristics at early stages and, ultimately, highly migratoryETS1+vascular smooth muscle cells. Together, our work establishes a single-cell chromatin-state framework for interpreting noncoding CHD risk variants and uncovers an ETS1-driven program linking Polycomb-deregulated noncoding variation to aberrant vascular smooth muscle fate commitment during human cardiogenesis.

title: Unveiling the underlying spin mechanism in quasi-2D perovskite spin-polarized lasing
abstract: Spin-polarized lasers hold great potential in integrated photonic devices for secure communication, optical interconnections, and advanced optical devices, offering excellent properties superior to those of conventional lasers. Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites are promising candidates for spin-polarized lasers, because their potential structural inversion asymmetry will result in strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) facilitating spin injection and hence spin splitting of electronic bands. However, strong SOC involves a trade-off between spin injection and spin lifetimes. How to prolong spin lifetimes in the lasing regime while maintaining the optical gain make it challenging to sustain spin polarization for lasing. Here, we unveil the underlying spin mechanism and successfully realize quasi-2D perovskite spin-polarized lasing by suppressing fast spin relaxation through triplet exciton regulation using organic cations of phenylethylammonium (PEA) and 1-naphthylmethylamine (NMA). We identify the Bir-Aronov-Pikus (BAP) mechanism is the dominant spin relaxation mechanism preventing the achievement of spin-polarized lasing in quasi-2D perovskites. By modulating the reverse intersystem crossing of triplet excitons, the D’yakonov-Perel’ (DP) mechanism becomes to play a key role and results in a new-emerged prolonged spin lifetime of 35.4 ps at 77 K, which is ∼5 times that of the BAP-induced one. Consequently, spin-polarized lasing is realized below 200 K, and the threshold is 30.2% lower than that for linearly polarized excitation. This work underscores the potential of PEA-based quasi-2D perovskites in spin-polarized lasing and contributes to the rapid advancements in perovskite spintronic devices.

title: Self-charged toothbrush facilitates tooth healthcare maintenance
abstract: Toothbrushes have undergone no substantive improvements beyond their mechanical function for about 1118 years to date. Conventional toothbrushes often fail to establish an antibacterial environment on the tooth surface, allowing bacteria to recover and recolonize. Here, we developed an innovative self-charged toothbrush that integrates daily tooth brushing with piezoelectric functionality, synergizing both optimal mechanical properties and stable electrical activity. The self-charged toothbrushes can generate reactive oxygen species to disrupt bacterial membrane integrity and diminish bacterial adhesion by combining static antibacterial inhibition through surface potential with dynamic piezoelectric stimulation. Clinical evaluation revealed that the localized piezoelectric stimulation of self-charged toothbrushes can mitigate plaque formation and gingival inflammation. Mechanistic studies further revealed that the self-charged toothbrushes induced oxidative damage to the oral pathogenic bacterial membranes, thereby impairing the ATP-binding cassette transporter pathway. Hence, this study developed a concept of piezoelectric PVDF toothbrushes that combine physical cleaning with sustained antibacterial effect, thus highlighting the potential of self-charged materials in advancing oral healthcare.

title: Thermalization of quantum light induced by classical nonlinear wave dynamics
abstract: Thermalization of isolated quantum systems is an intriguing phenomenon at the forefront of contemporary physics. In this work, we demonstrate that nonlinear multimode optical platforms can be harnessed to induce effective quantum interactions between photons. Through numerical experiments, we reveal the thermalization of quantum light, specifically single- and two-photon states, propagating alongside classical light within multimode nonlinear optical systems. This thermalization is clearly manifested by the emergence of Rayleigh-Jeans and Boltzmann statistical distributions. Beyond providing a deeper understanding of how classical nonlinearities can be used to investigate quantum many-body dynamics, our findings enable the exploration of a broader range of complex quantum phenomena, including aspects of quantum phase transitions, within readily accessible classical optical settings.

title: N6-methyladenosine–dependent ARv7 translation couples lactate metabolism with enzalutamide resistance in prostate cancer
abstract: Enzalutamide (Enz)–resistant prostate cancer (PCa) is a lethal disease that affects a broad population of elderly men. Experimental and clinical evidence has demonstrated that androgen receptor variant 7 (ARv7) plays a critical role in Enz-resistant (EnzR) PCa by functioning as a constitutively active transcription factor driving disease progression. However, the predictive value of the ARv7 transcript has not been fully recognized due to its low frequency in castration-resistant PCa. In this study, we identified ARv7 mRNA as anN6-methyladenosine (m6A)–modified transcript. Enz treatment increases METTL3-dependent m6A methylation of ARv7 mRNA at the A1177 site, which is subsequently recognized by the reader protein YTHDC2, leading to enhanced translation efficiency of ARv7. Furthermore, EnzR PCa exhibited elevated lactate metabolism, which regulated AR transcription through promoter-mediated epigenetic modifications at H3K9 and H3K14. Reactivated AR exhibited enhanced phase separation to transcriptionally up-regulate YTHDC2 expression. In vivo experiments demonstrated that targeting the METTL3-YTHDC2-ARv7 axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy to suppress EnzR PCa progression. Moreover, the METTL3 inhibitor STM2457 synergized with Enz to inhibit tumor growth without observable toxicity. Collectively, our findings suggest that the clinical utility of ARv7 may need to be reconsidered in light of its m6A-dependent translational regulation.

explanation: 该论文研究了古代玛雅人在古典期（公元250年至920年）面临的环境影响，特别是汞污染对水质量和生态系统的影响。研究通过沉积物核心中的汞浓度分析，证实了汞毒性是导致古代玛雅人口环境压力的额外因素。这与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测、大气成分分析等研究方向相关，因为汞作为一种污染物，其在大气和水体中的分布和影响是环境遥感技术的重要监测对象。
authors: Matthew Neal Waters;Savanna Lee Wooten;Ashley Mark Abrook;Mark Brenner;Jason Hilleary Curtis;Peter Guy Langdon;Roger Manuel Medina-Gonzalez;Savvas Paradeisis-Stathis;Richard Scott Vachula
title: Toxic mercury, aquatic ecosystem collapse, and the ancient Lowland Maya
abstract: Environmental impacts endured by the Lowland Maya during the Classic Period (250 to 920 CE) included droughts, deforestation, and soil erosion. Recent studies on mercury (Hg) pollution and cyanotoxins suggest that degraded water quality was also a stressor for the Pre-Columbian Maya. Hg in the Maya region is related to use of both elemental mercury and mineral cinnabar (HgS), the latter used as a red pigment. Questions, however, remain concerning the toxicity of Hg or the consequences of prehistoric Hg exposure on ecosystem and human health. Here, we show that Classic Period Hg concentrations in sediment cores from two lakes on the Yucatán Peninsula exceeded modern sediment Hg toxicity thresholds by orders of magnitude for centuries during ancient Maya occupation. Sediments also have evidence of aquatic food web collapse (algae, bacteria, cyanobacteria, ostracods, snails, and nonbiting midges), coincident with the time of high Hg concentrations, confirming that Hg toxicity was an additional environmental stressor for Classic Maya populations.

title: Independent origin of genomic imprinting in placental fish
abstract: Genomic imprinting results in biased expression of one parental allele. Such non-Mendelian expression occurs in angiosperms and placental mammals, which share having an active paternal genome during maternal offspring provisioning. It is hypothesized that imprinting modulates conflict between maternal control of resource allocation and paternal control of resource acquisition. If true, then imprinting should evolve in any organism that evolves a placenta. Here, we demonstrate genomic imprinting in a placental poeciliid fish,Poeciliopsis prolifica. Using transcriptomes from reciprocal crosses between two inbred strains, we identified 84 protein-coding genes with robust evidence of imprinting inP. prolificaplacenta. These include the teleost ortholog of mammalian imprinted gene,grb10, and a pair of adjacent genes,dpp4andgcga, with opposing effects on glucose metabolism that are oppositely imprinted in a fashion that potentially resolves parental conflict. Significantly elevated allelic DNA methylation on the promoters of two focal imprinted genes suggests epigenetic mechanisms of imprinting similar to those in mammals. We also discovered the convergent recruitment of a gene network associated with nutrient transport in mammals. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of genomic imprinting in a non-mammalian vertebrate and supports the potential role of imprinting in resolving parental conflict.

title: Cytoplasmic crowding drives intracellular viscoelastic increase during epithelial maturation
abstract: The cytoplasm is a crowded, active medium whose mechanical properties underpin essential cellular functions, yet how intracellular rheology adapts during tissue maturation remains unclear. Here, we examine the evolution of cytoplasmic viscoelasticity in Madin-Darby canine kidney epithelial monolayers as cell density increases. Using magnetic rotational spectroscopy, an active microrheology technique, we quantify zero-shear viscosity and elastic modulus throughout monolayer maturation. We uncover a substantial enhancement of intracellular viscoelasticity correlated with increasing cell density and a concomitant rise in cellular dry mass concentration. Hyperosmotic perturbations on subconfluent monolayers reproduce this effect, confirming cytoplasmic crowding as a driver of rheological changes. Notably, intracellular viscoelasticity scales linearly with dry mass concentration, suggesting a direct coupling between internal mechanics and cytoplasmic concentration during epithelial maturation. These findings establish a link between tissue-level organization and intracellular mechanics, highlighting cytoplasmic crowding as a regulator of epithelial homeostasis and providing a framework to connect rheology with tissue behavior.

title: IFNAR1 stabilization sustains CD8+ T cell persistence in IFN-high colorectal cancer liver metastases
abstract: Colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRC-LMs) are associated with poor survival and frequently resist immunotherapy, yet the mechanisms underlying this immune refractoriness remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify a tumor-intrinsic type I interferon (IFN-I)–high state in CRC-LMs associated with loss of the IFN-α/β receptor subunit 1 (IFNAR1) on effector T lymphocytes within immune-enriched perimetastatic niches. Reduced IFNAR1 expression stratifies patients with poor clinical outcomes. Transcriptional profiling of patient-derived organoids and complementary preclinical models revealed heterogeneous but recurrent tumor-derived IFN-I production in CRC-LMs. In IFN-Ihighcontexts, sustained signaling promoted IFNAR1 internalization on effector CD8+T cells, impairing their persistence, survival, and effector function. Pharmacologic or genetic stabilization of IFNAR1 on cell surface restored CD8+T cell fitness and selectively enhanced T cell receptor– and chimeric antigen receptor–based immunotherapies in IFN-Ihightumors. These findings define a context-dependent IFN-Ihigh/ IFNAR1lowaxis that constrains antitumor immunity in CRC-LMs and identify IFNAR1 stabilization as a strategy to convert chronic IFN signaling from a suppressive barrier into a therapeutic vulnerability.

title: Pancreatic α cells function as MHC class II–dependent antigen-presenting cells in type 1 diabetes
abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an autoimmune disease characterized by T cell–mediated destruction of pancreatic β cells, in which antigen presentation is essential. Although professional antigen-presenting cells initiate autoreactive T cell responses, whether endocrine cells contribute to antigen presentation within inflamed islets remains unclear. Here, we show that pancreatic α cells acquire major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II (MHC-II)–dependent antigen-presenting capacity during T1D progression. Reanalysis of single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from nonobese diabetic (NOD) mice and human T1D islets revealed progressive up-regulation of MHC-II associated genes in α cells. Immunostaining validated the increased of MHC-II level both in NOD mice and patients with T1D. Mechanistically, inflammatory cytokines activated the Janus kinase–signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT) pathway in α cells, leading to JAK-STAT–dependent MHC-II induction. Functionally, activated α cells internalized, processed, and presented exogenous antigens, acquired expression of costimulatory molecules, and promoted antigen-specific CD4+T cell activation. These findings identify pancreatic α cells as nonprofessional antigen-presenting cells and expand the current understanding of antigen presentation in autoimmune diabetes.

title: Rapid, voxel-based 3D printing with yield-stress fluid inks
abstract: Despite decades of progress, 3D printing still presents trade-offs in what materials can be printed and at what resolutions, speeds, and part volumes. We introduce direct ink additive lithography, or DIAL, to alleviate these trade-offs when printing with yield-stress, complex fluid inks used to print functional materials. DIAL combines translational photopatterning with ink sheet deposition for rapid, voxel-based 3D printing. Using model DIAL inks with kilopascal-scale yield stresses, we evaluate how ink rheology influences printing and compare DIAL against digital light processing (DLP) and direct ink writing (DIW). Since DIAL enables fast, high-throughput, support-free, and large-area printing, we showcase its broad potential for producing functional materials by printing multiscale architected, multimaterial, structural electrolyte, and hydrogel structures that are difficult if not impossible to 3D print today.

title: A biofilm-derived peptide as an underwater adhesive
abstract: Wet adhesives that perform under water have broad applications in industrial and biomedical settings. To date, molecular designs for underwater adhesives have largely been inspired by marine animals including mussels and barnacles. Here, we propose bacterial biofilms as an alternative source of inspiration for underwater adhesives. Specifically, we demonstrate the application potential of a peptide derived from biofilms formed by the notorious pathogenVibrio cholerae. We characterize the ability of this biofilm-derived peptide to adsorb onto various surfaces and to glue wet surfaces by using a combination of confocal microscopy, molecular dynamics simulations, atomic force microscopy, lap shear tests, and spectroscopic tools. We further show that the peptide can coaggregate with microspheres acting as an effective flocculant. Our results open new design possibilities for underwater adhesives inspired by natural biofilms.

title: A high robustness decoding technique for ultrasound modulated electroencephalogram
abstract: Ultrasound-modulated electroencephalography (USMEEG) has become a vital tool in neuroscience because it integrates millimeter-level spatial resolution with millisecond-level temporal resolution. However, under extremely complex scenarios, excessively strong or weak acoustoelectric signal coupling leads to severe distortion in USMEEG decoded signals. To address this, we developed a highly robust decoding algorithm based on the ultrasound pulse repetition frequency and introduced the acoustoelectric modulation ratio (AMR) to quantify different modulation scenarios. Across numerical simulations, phantoms, and validation using human steady-state visual evoked potential signals with data-level acoustoelectric coupling across 10 volunteers, the focused ultrasound phased array achieved an encoding spatial resolution of 0.79 millimeters. The proposed algorithm significantly outperformed four traditional methods, exhibiting higher precision under weak modulation (0 < AMR ≤ 0.6), moderate modulation (0.6 < AMR ≤ 1), and over modulation (AMR > 1) conditions, with average decoding correlations reaching 0.84, 0.90, and 0.89. This highly robust technique expands USMEEG applications and provides a technical foundation for high-performance noninvasive brain-computer interfaces.

title: Effector-triggered stomatal immunity prevents leaf invasion by bacterial pathogens
abstract: The phytopathogenPseudomonas syringaemust enter the leaf interior through natural openings such as stomata to cause disease. Plants restrict pathogen entry into the leaf through non–self-recognition–driven stomatal closure.P. syringaecounters this stomatal immunity by deploying a range of toxins and effectors. Here, we show that stomatal immunity inArabidopsis thalianais reinforced upon recognition of the ubiquitousP. syringaetype III effector AvrE1 by the resistance protein CAR1.CAR1expression is enriched in guard cells, and its activation prolongs the effective duration of stomatal immunity. We also show that CAR1 prevents the invasion of leaf tissue by natural isolates ofP. syringae, demonstrating that stomatal immunity provides a broadly significant barrier to host accessibility byP. syringaethat carry the conserved effector AvrE1.

title: Dynamic redox reactivation of platinum sites for long-term glycolate electrosynthesis from polyethylene terephthalate wastes
abstract: Glycolates are indispensable in the health, chemical and pharmaceutical industries, whereas their mainstream production involve toxic chemicals and harsh operating condition. An alternative route for glycolate production is electrifying ethylene glycol (EG) that originates from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) but suffers from poor durability of active platinum site that tend to deactivate. Herein, we demonstrate a dynamic redox reactivation strategy, which alternates between working potential for oxidizing EG to glycolate and nonworking potential for reviving active platinum sites by the chemical reduction of adsorbed EG, realizing an unprecedented stability for over 3000 hours under average current density of ∼220 milliamperes per square centimeter. Upscaling this approach, the assembled electrolyzer drives a record current of 10 amperes at 1.18 volts for repeatable 40 batches of glycolates electrosynthesis, with each batch converting 48.0 grams of PET to 11.6 grams of glycolates (52.8% yield), 37.7 grams ofp-phthalic acid (95.8% yield), 248.7 grams of NaHSO4(95.2% yield) and ∼11.5 liters of hydrogen, showcasing a considerable revenue of ∼$1072 per ton glycolate.

title: Massively parallel self-assembly of suspendable microcompartments for functional cell screening
abstract: Modern biology increasingly demands platforms that can compartmentalize and analyze single cells and cell-cell interactions at massive scale, yet existing compartmentalization strategies based on microfluidics suffer from critical limitations. Emerging lab-on-a-particle technologies such as nanovials enable anchored single cells or small groups of cells to be isolated and assayed in a fully suspendable and parallelized manner using standard instrumentation, although their open architectures can result in loss of growing or un-attached cells. Here, we introduce capped nanovials: self-assembling hydrogel compartments formed by docking spherical capping particles into bowl-shaped nanovials. We routinely achieve capping of >80% of all nanovials in a sample and >90% sorting yield by flow cytometry, making the capped nanovial system well-suited for preparing and running large-scale assays. Furthermore, we demonstrate stable clonal expansion of single mammalian, yeast, and bacterial cells; growth-based selections of >10,000 colonies; enhanced signal-to-noise in secretion assays; and high-purity selection of antibody-secreting cells based on activation of co-encapsulated T cell reporters (>30-fold signal, up to 100% selection purity). By combining the simplicity of a well plate with the functional precision of droplet microfluidics without requiring oil or custom instrumentation, capped nanovials realize accessible, high-throughput, and high-resolution experimentation.

title: Human carotid plaque risk imaging using multiparametric photoacoustic and ultrasound fusion (hCAPRI)
abstract: Assessing the risk of carotid plaque rupture remains limited because current imaging methods cannot provide both plaque composition and structural information in real time. Here, we present human carotid plaque risk imaging (hCAPRI), a multiparametric photoacoustic and ultrasound (PA/US) fusion method for real-time carotid plaque assessment. hCAPRI combines PA imaging for detecting intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) with US imaging for evaluating the plaque structure. PA imaging measured IPH size and methemoglobin content, while US imaging assessed stenosis severity, calcification, and plaque thickness. Combining these PA/US parameters, we compute an hCAPRI score. In 171 carotid arteries (CAs) from 120 patients, hCAPRI revealed the relationships among the PA/US parameters. In 36 CAs validated with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), hCAPRI showed high agreement with MRI. The hCAPRI score achieved 89% sensitivity and 84% specificity for high-risk plaque classification. hCAPRI offers a low-cost, real-time, and contrast-free approach for carotid plaque risk imaging.

title: Lighting up necrotic neurons from traumatic brain injury with magnetic quantum dots to decode the cellular origin of MRI
abstract: The diagnosis of traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains heavily constrained by the limitations of conventional imaging techniques in visualizing the pathological events that determine the disease progression and outcome. To address this clinical challenge, we report a manganese-doped near-infrared quantum dot (QD) to intrinsically integrate the highly sensitive optical imaging with clinical compatible magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Taking the advantages of optical imaging powered by whole-brain clearing and cellular resolution three-dimensional (3D) panoptic imaging, in combination with the systematic in vitro cell studies on different types of cells involved in TBI, we disclosed the interpretable pathology reflected by TBI imaging through the highly sensitive fluorescence of magnetic QDs, i.e., after systemic administration, the nanoprobes were extravasated through the compromised blood-brain barrier and then selectively phagocytosed by activated microglia, which subsequently migrated into the regions rich in dead neurons and neuronal debris. This microglia-mediated tropism decodes the signal origin of MRI enhanced by the nanometer-sized contrast agent, thereby transforming the MRI from an anatomical tool into a pathological reporter. A biocompatible Fe3O4nanoparticle of similar size was also compared with the magnetic QD mentioned above for validating the translational merits of nanoparticles in MRI diagnosis of TBI.

title: Mechano-electrochemical energy harvesting and self-powered sensing via dynamic liquid metal–electrolyte interfaces
abstract: Wearable devices, stretchable sensors, and soft electronics benefit from harvesting ambient energy using compliant materials, yet existing approaches often face limitations in power density, scalability, and electrode adaptability. Here, we report a liquid metal mechano-electrochemical energy harvester (LMMEEH) that converts mechanical stimuli into electricity through dynamically regulated electrode-electrolyte interfaces. Mechanical motion changes the interfacial area and drives asymmetric Faradaic reactions associated with dynamic oxide formation and dissolution, generating electrical output. The fluidity, high surface tension, and self-renewing surface chemistry of liquid metals enable rapid interfacial reformation, large reversible deformation, and stable cyclic operation. The device achieves a power density of 140.2 microwatts per square meter and scales to a 40-unit array producing 2 volts. Spatial and temporal programming of the liquid metal interfaces further enables synchronized three-phase alternating-current generation. We demonstrate wave-driven emergency lighting, self-powered pressure sensing, and real-time physiological monitoring. This work establishes dynamic liquid metal electrochemical interfaces as a scalable strategy for soft mechanical energy harvesting and self-powered electronics.

title: Rapid activation kinetics of the NLR Swordholder underpin nonhost resistance to Phytophthora capsici in Nicotiana tabacum
abstract: Nonhost resistance (NHR) represents a durable phenomenon where plants resist nonadapted pathogens. While NHR holds substantial potential for engineering crops with broad-spectrum and durable resistance, its underlying molecular mechanism remains incompletely understood. The oomycete pathogenPhytophthora capsiciis nonadapted toNicotiana tabacum(Nt) but is virulent on the closely relatedNicotiana benthamiana(Nb). Here, we demonstrated that both species encode the NLR Swordholder (Swh), which recognizesP. capsiciAvrNt effector proteins. NtSwh restores NHR inntswhmutants, whereas NbSwh confers only partial resistance. Mechanistically, NtSwh exhibits weaker autoinhibition mediated by its amino-terminal extension domains, enabling rapid immune signaling that prevent pathogen effector–mediated suppression; NbSwh’s stronger autoinhibition delays activation, permitting effector suppression. Heterologous expression of NtSwh in tomato enhances field resistance toP. capsiciwithout yield penalty. These findings indicate that the kinetics of NLR can play a key role in defining NHR, in addition to the presence or absence of specific NLRs, providing insights into strategies for breeding durable crop immunity.

title: Direct regulation of a tRNA modification enzyme by ppGpp links stress signaling to translational control and biofilm development
abstract: Transfer RNA (tRNA) modifications influence decoding efficiency and translational fidelity, yet how they are integrated into bacterial signaling networks remains poorly understood. Here, we identify a direct connection between stress signaling and codon-specific translational regulation. We show that the alarmone guanosine tetraphosphate (ppGpp) directly inhibits MnmE (TrmE), a conserved tRNA-modification GTPase required for methylaminomethyl (mnm) modification of wobble uridine. High-resolution ribosome profiling inBacillus subtilisrevealed that loss of MnmE selectively increases ribosome pausing at AAG codons and reprograms translation of a subset of genes, including small open reading frames. Among these is a previously unrecognized AAG-containing leader peptide that controls expression of the biofilm repressor AbrB. Consistent with this mechanism,mnmEmutants exhibit constitutive extracellular matrix production and bypass the biofilm defect of arelAmutant. Together, these findings establish a pathway linking ppGpp signaling, tRNA modification, codon-specific translation, and multicellular development.

title: A disynaptic trigeminal circuit for the transformation and integration of oral chemesthesis in male mice
abstract: Chemesthesis, encompassing oral sensations such as spiciness and coolness, is an important yet incompletely understood component of mammalian chemical sensing. Unlike taste or olfaction, these sensations are conveyed primarily through trigeminal pathways; however, how modality-specific peripheral signals are processed and transformed along central ascending pathways remains poorly understood. Herein, we delineate the structural and functional organization of an ascending trigeminal-brainstem-parabrachial circuit that mediates oral chemesthetic processing in male mice. Using viral tracing, in vivo calcium imaging, and chemogenetic and optogenetic manipulations, we identify a genetically defined disynaptic glutamatergic pathway (trigeminal ganglion → spinal trigeminal nucleus caudalis → lateral parabrachial nucleus) that is both necessary and sufficient for capsaicin- and menthol-evoked defensive behaviors. Although peripheral TRPV1+and TRPM8+neurons retain a degree of modality bias, we observe substantial convergence of spicy and cooling signals within the spinal trigeminal nucleus, followed by sustained and synchronized population activity invglut2+neurons of the external lateral parabrachial nucleus. This hierarchical transformation from peripheral segregation to central integration reveals the organizational principle by which distinct chemesthetic modalities are progressively integrated along a trigeminal-mediated ascending pathway, providing a circuit-level framework for understanding how chemical stimuli are processed and coordinated to drive defensive behaviors.

explanation: 该论文主要研究冠状病毒S蛋白的结构动力学及其与温度和受体结合的协调激活机制，涉及病毒学、生物物理学等领域，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演等）没有直接关联。
authors: Jiaming Liang;Cheng Peng;Ruixiao Tan;Yutong Song;Zheyuan Zhang;Jinfang Yu;Xinquan Wang;Sai Li
title: On-virion structural dynamics reveal temperature- and receptor-coordinated activation of an alphacoronavirus spike
abstract: Human alphacoronaviruses primarily infect the human upper respiratory tract, yet how temperature and receptor-binding coordinate viral spike (S) protein activation remains unclear. Using cryo-electron tomography and subtomogram averaging, we directly visualized the structural dynamics of S on human coronavirus 229E (HCoV-229E) virions under physiologically relevant temperatures and in the presence of the host receptor human aminopeptidase N (hAPN). We identified two prefusion S2 conformations, compact and loose, that interconvert reversibly by temperature, revealing intrinsic S2 “breathing” on virions. Receptor-binding domain (RBD)-up conformations are rare on apo virions but are promoted at 33°C and stabilized upon receptor binding. hAPN can bind bivalently to neighboring S, forming Gemini S-hAPN complexes. Receptor incubation further promotes conversion from prefusion to postfusion S, an effect enhanced at 33°C. Together, our results demonstrate an optimized temperature for the HCoV-229E viral fitness, and establish temperature and receptor binding as synergistic regulators of alphacoronavirus S activation. These findings provide a structural framework for understanding alphacoronavirus infectivity.

explanation: 该论文主要研究西伯利亚榴辉岩金刚石中的氧逸度、温度和压力，以及它们对太古代对流地幔氧化状态的意义。虽然涉及地球科学和环境科学中的某些概念，但与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）没有直接关系。
authors: Giulia Marras;Denis Mikhailenko;Catherine A. McCammon;Sonja Aulbach;Yuhang Lu;Renbiao Tao;Alla Logvinova;Dmitry Zedgenizov;Vincenzo Stagno
title: Oxygen fugacity, temperature, and pressure of Siberian eclogitic diamonds: Implications for the Archaean convecting mantle redox state
abstract: Kimberlite-borne eclogite xenoliths ultimately derive from ancient subducted oceanic crust. Some specimens still record the chemical and redox conditions of their igneous protoliths, allowing a view into contemporaneous convecting mantle sources. However, accurate reconstructions are limited because eclogites have been exposed to metasomatism in the subcontinental mantle for billions of years. Here, we investigated garnet and clinopyroxene inclusions, both touching and nontouching pairs, in 19 eclogitic diamonds from the Siberian craton, hence shielded from post-entrapment overprint. Inclusion compositions indicate average sampling depths of 180 to 280 km, temperatures of 1030° to 1540°C (±60°C), and redox conditions, for most of the samples, oxidized enough for diamonds to have originated from water(carbonate)-rich fluids. The reconstructed bulk composition points to basaltic oceanic crust formed from an Archaean convecting mantle region that was more oxygen-depleted than today, providing compelling evidence of redox heterogeneities in the source rocks of ancient oceanic crust.

explanation: 该论文主要研究GHz飞秒脉冲驱动下的自由基累积及其在超疏水转换中的应用，涉及材料科学和化学领域，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演等）无关。
authors: Junke Huang;Jiachen Yin;Shupeng Xu;Tao Yuan;Tianjun Yao;Zhen Zhang;Mengyun Hu;Heping Zeng
title: Accumulated radicals by GHz femtosecond burst drive one-step superhydrophobic conversion
abstract: Short-lived radicals usually decay before they can drive long-range reactions, making laser-induced radical chain reactions difficult to sustain. Here, we used GHz femtosecond bursts to temporally couple excitation events, allowing reactive intermediates from preceding subpulses to remain available for subsequent reactions and favoring their transient accumulation relative to isolated-pulse excitation. Consistent with this temporally coupled process, the methylphenyl silicone resin/graphene/CuFe2O4/SiO2composite coating exhibits a threshold-like nonlinear wettability transition near 430 subpulses. Compared with the microsecond-spaced single-pulse femtosecond regime, the sub-nanosecond GHz burst produces more extensive chemical conversion, enabling one-step bond reorganization and phase transformation and yielding a low-adhesion superhydrophobic surface with a contact angle of 161° ± 0.7° without posttreatment. Pulse-timing–controlled radical-mediated chemistry thus provides a time-domain strategy for ultrafast materials synthesis.

explanation: 该论文主要关注霍乱的传播动力学和流行病学分析，未涉及大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析或气溶胶反演等。
authors: Bethany L. DiPrete;Javier Perez-Saez;Shirlee Wohl;Nathaniel Matteson;Seungwon Kim;Andrew S. Azman;Justin Lessler
title: Defining epidemiologically relevant units of cholera transmission in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Much remains unknown about cholera transmission dynamics in Africa. Applying both traditional phylogeographic techniques and innovative methods for combining epidemiologic and genomic data, we identified three to four distinct “cholera transmission units” within which cross-border cholera transmission has been more frequent. These units can be grouped into two major transmission clusters, one in Western Africa and bordering countries and one spanning the Central, Eastern, and Southern regions. Simulation studies show that these clusters can be used to assess the risk of international spread of introduced cholera strains and identify heterogeneities in the speed of international spread based on outbreak location. Our methods further allow us to infer cholera incidence attributable to specific lineages in the absence of sequencing data. This work has clear implications for cholera control.
